stack:
A Bun/TypeScript monorepo with 14 packages: aws-lambda, cli, core, engine, gcp-cloud-run, lint, parsers, player, producer, sdk, sdk-playground, shader-transitions, studio and studio-server.

- **Rendering:** puppeteer / puppeteer-core plus FFmpeg. Chrome BeginFrame capture runs on Linux only; other platforms fall back to Page.captureScreenshot.
- **Animation:** GSAP, which the studio depends on and which registry items load from the CDN.
- **Transcription:** embedded-captions/transcribe.cjs defaults to WhisperX through `uvx` (Python, pinned whisperx==3.8.6), falling back to whisper.cpp. The CLI also offers Parakeet-MLX.
- **Matting:** u2net_human_seg through onnxruntime-node. It auto-selects CoreML on Apple Silicon or CUDA, otherwise CPU.
- **Color grading:** a WebGL shader.
- **Agent skills:** 21 top-level skills/*/SKILL.md (40 SKILL.md files repo-wide), plus plugin manifests for Claude Code, Codex and Cursor.
- **Registry:** 165 blocks and 223 components.
- **Studio:** a React NLE with 15 WebMCP tool files.

summary:
The slug and repo are real, and they are very active: 3 releases in the last day and commits every hour. Most of the first review's claims hold up when checked against the code. Several details were wrong or overstated, and one of them bears directly on the relayed question ("AutoBroll has captions, but not Captions.ai-level ones").

**Caption engine.** The premium caption engine really exists and is deep. skills/embedded-captions has three compilers, 25 themes plus 10 DNAs (35 styles), per-word animations for every rail style, and hero words placed behind the subject using a person matte. Heroes in the cinematic/DNA path get entrance strength coupled to real loudness (lib-dna.cjs reads envelope.json). QA gates cover timing, occlusion and overflow.

**It is not reel-ready as shipped:**
- The theme compiler defaults to 1280x720 and the cinematic compiler to 1920x1080.
- There is no emoji system. caption-emoji-pop is a 1920x1080 demo with a hard-coded transcript and a 7-word emoji map.
- The skill refuses footage with hard cuts and multi-shot clips, and ships the footage untouched (no grading).
- The Studio "caption designer" animation presets (entrance, highlight, exit, stagger) are stored but never reach the render. generator.ts emits only a 0.2 s group fade.
- The first review took the matting speed ("CPU-only, about 2 fps") from a stale SKILL.md. The code auto-selects CoreML on Apple Silicon, and the matte.cjs header says about 9 fps.

**Motion graphics.** The motion-graphics registry is large and real: 165 blocks and 223 components of GSAP HTML, plus a director, builder and verify skill pipeline. But 151 of the 165 blocks are 16:9. Only 14 are portrait, mostly chat and social UI mockups, and all 11 lower-thirds are landscape.

**Color grading.** A real WebGL grading engine with LUTs, wheels, curves and 18 presets.

**Weak spots:**
- Cutting is a transcript cut-list compiler with no retake detection and no VAD.
- There is no stock video. Image and icon search go only through HeyGen's own CLI, and there is no Pexels provider.

**LLM harness.** An almost exact match for a Claude Code or Codex brain.

**New license risks:**
- Commercial fonts (TT Norms Pro, ABC Solar Display) are committed in the .agents/ and .claude/ changelog-video skills.
- The npm engine package declares no license.

**Answer to the relayed question:** yes, HyperFrames is the strongest donor for closing AutoBroll's premium-caption gap. Specifically, lift skills/embedded-captions (compilers, DNA and theme presets, matte, safe-zones and gates) under Apache-2.0. Budget for three pieces of work:
- 9:16 retuning.
- An emoji layer.
- Running captions after the cut, since the skill assumes single-shot footage.

Do not count on the Studio caption designer or the caption-* registry snippets. They are shallow templates.

fit_rationale:
The architecture matches the user's plan: a Claude Code or Codex brain, deterministic CLI tools, locked compilers, a deterministic renderer, and skills already packaged for both agents. Captions, motion-graphics infrastructure, grading and rendering are the strongest of any open-source candidate.

I lowered the score from 7 to 6 for five reasons:
1. Forking an 8k-file repo that ships several releases a day means constant drift.
2. The talking-head skills assume untouched, single-shot footage. The premium caption skill refuses hard cuts, and nothing orchestrates cut, then grade, then caption, then B-roll.
3. The premium captions and 92% of the motion-graphics blocks default to landscape, and there is no emoji layer.
4. The Studio caption-animation UI does not reach the render.
5. Cutting has no retake detection, and there is no stock-video provider.

The better plan is to depend on the `hyperframes` CLI or engine (after resolving the missing license field on @hyperframes/engine) and write a thin 9:16 reels skill pack. That pack would sit on the cut-list, grading, embedded-captions and registry pieces, plus a Pexels provider. Alternatively, lift embedded-captions directly into AutoBroll as a donor.

captions_detail:
Everything below was checked against the code. Nothing was rendered.

**1. skills/embedded-captions (the real premium engine)**

Pipeline: prepare.sh runs matte, transcribe and audio-envelope in parallel, then safe-zones. The agent authors theme.json or cinematic.json, a locked compiler builds the HTML, preview-frames.cjs renders QA stills, and render-and-composite.sh produces the final video.
- The caption model is drop (filler), rail (verbatim lower-third with inline emphasis) or embed (a hero word behind the subject via the u2net matte), with apex and minor hero tiers.
- There are 35 identities: 25 themes and 10 DNAs.
- The theme rails each have their own per-word verb, such as splitflap, LED wipe, igniteconverge, paste, per-character hammer, coinpop, trackglitch and scribble. Emphasis words get their own treatment.
- Theme compilers write plate reactions (punch, shake, grain) to _postfx.sh.
- In the cinematic/DNA path, hero amplitude follows real RMS loudness.
- Gates check timing, occlusion and overflow.

Limits for reels:
- Defaults are landscape (1280x720 for themes, 1920x1080 for cinematic), and positions are in pixels.
- There is no emoji.
- It refuses multi-shot or hard-cut footage and leaves the footage untouched.
- Transcription defaults to WhisperX (multilingual `small`) through uvx, falling back to whisper.cpp; Spanish is fine.
- Matting runs about 9 fps on CoreML on Apple Silicon.

**2. registry/components/caption-* (17)**

These are 1920x1080 demo compositions with hard-coded transcripts. Examples: pill-karaoke (per-word active color), emoji-pop (a 7-word map, group animation) and kinetic-slam. They are useful as style references, not as an engine.

**3. Studio caption designer**

It edits per-word style, and the runtime applies those style overrides. The entrance, highlight, exit and stagger animation presets are stored but never emitted; the generator only fades groups.

**Bottom line for AutoBroll:** lift embedded-captions (compilers, DNA and theme JSONs, lib-dna, safe-zones, matte, gates). Then add three things: a 9:16 retune, an emoji layer, and a step that runs it on the already-cut edit.
motion_graphics_detail:
Graphics are HTML and CSS animated with GSAP (Lottie, Three.js, WAAPI and Anime.js adapters are also available) and rendered deterministically in Chrome.

**Templates.** The registry has 165 blocks and 223 components, all real registry-item.json entries.
- 151 blocks are 1920x1080. 14 are portrait or near-portrait, mostly chat and social UI mockups (chatgpt-exchange, claude-exchange, tiktok-follow, instagram-follow, notification-cascade, spotify-card).
- All 11 lt-* lower-thirds are 16:9.
- Components are size-agnostic snippets, e.g. count-up, headline-slam, push-in, camera-shake, confetti.
- Previews are mp4s on HeyGen's CDN.

**LLM-authored graphics.** Two skills drive this:
- skills/motion-graphics: a director subagent plans, a builder subagent builds reuse-first with `hyperframes add`, then lint, check and snapshot contact sheets run, with a repair pass on failure.
- skills/talking-head-recut: storyboard.json with 5 zones on a 16:9, 9:16 or 4:5 canvas, 10 style, 4 layout and 3 frame reference HTMLs, adapted from the MIT project vtake-skills.

**SFX.** 19 bundled Pixabay mp3s with a manifest, falling back to HeyGen's audio catalog (network).

**Output.** Transparent overlays render through ProRes 4444 or VP9 alpha.

Visual quality was not verified by rendering.
llm_integration_detail:
The integration is skills-first and works with any agent.
- **Plugins:** .claude-plugin, .codex-plugin (skills: ./skills/) and .cursor-plugin manifests, plus scripts/package-codex-plugin.mjs to build the Codex plugin.
- **Skills:** 21 top-level skills route through /hyperframes. They call the CLI (about 50 commands, many with --json) and Node compilers.
- **No API keys in the core.** No core package depends on an LLM SDK. codex-provider.mjs shells out to the `codex` CLI for optional image generation.
- **Remote options:** the Studio exposes 15 WebMCP tool files, and a hosted HeyGen MCP is documented in docs/guides/mcp.mdx (needs a HeyGen account).
- **The agent authors the creative JSON:** theme.json, cinematic.json, storyboard.json, shot-plan.json and cut ranges.
- **Side effects:** `hyperframes init` checks GitHub and refreshes the global skills in ~/.claude/skills and ~/.agents/skills. Telemetry is on by default (the telemetry config comments say 'default: true in production').

summary:
Direct answer: yes. AutoBroll has real, working captions, but they are not Captions.ai/Submagic-class. src/CaptionTrack.tsx (103 lines) draws one hard-coded look:
- Font is Inter at 62px, weight 600 (800 for accent words), with a double text-shadow.
- The word being spoken switches from 78% white to white and jumps to scale(1.05) with no easing.
- The words Gemini picks as accents are drawn in one accent color for the whole page.
- Each page fades in and slides up 10px, and fades out.

It has no per-word entrance animation, no emoji, no presets, no font choice, and no box, stroke or highlight pill. The "Styles" tab in editor/Inspector.tsx is just 6 accent-color swatches (ACCENT_SWATCHES).

What it does well on captions is the plumbing:
- phrase-aware paging
- LLM-picked accent words
- face-aware vertical placement (Gemini vision on one frame per source)
- captions anchored to clips, so they survive trims, reorders and speed changes

The rest of the app:
- **Cutting:** silence only, from WhisperX word gaps over 600ms.
- **Retakes:** only as a whole-file "best take" suggestion from Gemini.
- **B-roll:** Gemini-planned Pexels stock or the creator's own footage.
- **Motion graphics:** none. **Color grade:** none.
- **In-app AI:** hard-wired to Gemini.

The strongest asset for the user's harness idea is mcp/server.mjs, a real stdio MCP server with 24 zod-typed tools. They edit clips, captions, B-roll and music, run the AI steps, render, and return frames to look at. The tools are already registered in this user's Claude Code session (mcp__autobroll__*).

Two caveats, both in mcp/server.mjs:
- set_keyframes documents x/y as pixels, but the renderer treats them as percent.
- No tool gives per-word timestamps.

Spanish does not work out of the box, because lib-transcribe.mjs:48 hard-codes `--language en`.
captions_detail:
**Generation** (scripts/captions-multiclip.mjs + scripts/lib-transcribe.mjs):
- WhisperX `medium` runs with `--language en` hard-coded (lib-transcribe.mjs:48). The default initial_prompt also says English.
- Word timestamps are cached per source file.
- buildCaptions() starts a new page:
  - at MAX_WORDS=5, or MAX_WORDS+2 when the line would end on a glue word;
  - on pauses over 450ms (GAP_MS);
  - at sentence and clause punctuation;
  - at clip boundaries.
- It won't end a line on a GLUE word, but GLUE is an English-only word list. A one-word orphan within 350ms merges into the previous page.
- detectAccents(): Gemini structured output asks for 5-12% "meaning" words.
- detectFaces(): one 540px ffmpeg frame per source goes to Gemini for a face box. faceToTop() then puts the block chin+5%, or above the head when the face sits low, clamped between 8% and 72%. Results are cached per source.

**Render** (src/CaptionTrack.tsx):
- One Remotion Sequence per page. The page fades in over 0.14s with a 10px upward slide and fades out over 0.18s.
- A page holds until whichever comes first: the next page, end+700ms, or the clip end.
- Per word:
  - color: the accent color if accented, else white while spoken, else rgba(255,255,255,0.78)
  - scale(1.05) when active or accented, applied instantly with no interpolation
  - the same double text-shadow on every word

**Missing** (verified by grep: no emoji, spring, stroke or box code anywhere in src/):
- per-word entrance animation (pop, bounce, typewriter or karaoke fill)
- emoji and keyword stickers
- style presets and font choice
- background box, stroke, or an animated highlight pill
- emphasis levels beyond one accent flag

**Font bug:** Inter is loaded only in editor/index.html (Google Fonts, weights 400-700). It is not loaded in the Remotion bundle (src/index.ts only calls registerRoot). The preview synthesizes weight 800, and the exported mp4 uses a system font unless Inter happens to be installed.

**Editing:**
- UI: caption text (textarea), accent toggles per word, vertical position (slider, or drag on the preview) and scale.
- MCP: edit_caption and add_caption.
- Retyped text is re-timed evenly across the page (retext()), not re-aligned to the audio.
- Caption timing cannot be changed on the timeline. The caption track only selects and seeks, even though the header comment in Timeline.tsx says "drag block = move, drag edges = retime".

**Verdict:** good timing, anchoring and placement under a deliberately minimal look; the README itself pitches a "sparing" aesthetic. Getting to Submagic quality means:
- rewriting CaptionTrack.tsx into a preset and animation engine (spring, font loading, stroke/box/pill);
- extending CaptionWord {text, startMs, endMs, accent} with emphasis level, emoji and style id;
- making paging and GLUE language-aware.
motion_graphics_detail:
There are none. The repo has:
- no motion-graphics templates;
- no LLM-authored Remotion or HTML components;
- no kinetic typography, animated stats, icons, lower thirds, UI mockups, transitions or SFX. A grep for spring(, emoji, sfx, whoosh and lower third across src, scripts, server, mcp and editor finds nothing.

The only animation primitives are:
1. Per-clip zoom/pan keyframes. src/timeline.ts sampleTransform() does smoothstep interpolation of scale/x/y by source time, and src/MultiClipVideo.tsx ClipMedia applies it as `translate(x%, y%) scale(s)`. It is editable on the preview (drag = pan, corner = zoom keyframe) and through MCP set_keyframes. An agent could use it to write zoom punches by hand, but nothing generates them. Also, the set_keyframes description says x/y are "px of the 1080x1920 frame" while the renderer and editor use percent, so an agent following the doc would push the clip off-screen.
2. A 0.18s fade-in on B-roll (src/Broll.tsx). There is no fade-out.
3. The caption page fade and slide.

A motion-graphics layer would fit the architecture as another clip-anchored Sequence track, like projectBrolls, but all of it would be new work.
llm_integration_detail:
There are two separate layers.

**(1) In-app AI is hard-wired to Gemini.** scripts/gemini.mjs sends a raw fetch to generativelanguage.googleapis.com with `?key=` in the URL, uses responseSchema structured output at temperature 0.2, and has retry on 429/503 in the callers. Three pipeline scripts call it:
- arrange-clips.mjs: orders clips and picks the "best" take
- captions-multiclip.mjs: detectAccents plus detectFaces (vision)
- broll-multiclip.mjs: plans B-roll moments

There is no provider abstraction, so Claude or Codex cannot drive these steps without replacing gemini.mjs. The prompts and schemas are short and easy to port.

**(2) External agent through MCP.** mcp/server.mjs (McpServer + StdioServerTransport) registers exactly 24 tools, which I counted:

list_projects, get_project, duplicate_project, rename_project, set_accent_color, add_clips, reorder_clips, trim_clip, set_clip, delete_clips, split_clip, set_keyframes, edit_caption, add_caption, delete_captions, search_stock, add_broll, edit_broll, delete_brolls, set_music, run_ai_step (arrange | autocut | captions | broll through backend jobs, polled), render (draft or full), frame_at (returns an image content block), health.

- Edits go through POST /api/projects/:id when the backend is up and write the JSON file directly otherwise.
- The editor polls updatedAt and live-reloads.
- .mcp.json auto-registers the server for Claude Code inside the repo. This user's session already lists the mcp__autobroll__* tools.

Gaps for the harness idea:
- get_project prints only each caption page's start time, not per-word timestamps. There is no transcript tool, so agent-driven filler or retake cuts at word precision need raw file reads of public/clips/transcripts/<source>.json, which Claude Code can do in-repo.
- The set_keyframes pixel/percent documentation bug (see motion_graphics_detail).
- run_ai_step still needs a GEMINI_API_KEY.
- Codex CLI is never mentioned in the repo. Codex does support stdio MCP servers through config.toml, so it should connect, but that is inferred and untested, including whether Codex shows frame_at's image results.
- No skills, no Agent SDK, no headless `claude -p` or `codex exec` wiring.

Net: Claude Code can already be the editing brain over deterministic tools. The "agent decides, tool executes" split is half there.

fit_rationale:
The shape is right for the harness idea, and it is small enough (about 4.6k lines) to own completely. The pieces:
- a JSON project model with clip-anchored overlays;
- one Remotion composition shared by preview and export;
- deterministic pipelines as spawnable scripts;
- a CapCut-like UI with live reload;
- most valuable, a working 24-tool MCP server that Claude Code already mounts.

But what it does well (WhisperX timing, silence cut, Pexels B-roll, face-aware placement, ducking) is the cheaper half. The user's differentiators are missing or minimal:
- **Premium captions:** one fixed minimal style; CaptionTrack.tsx needs a full rewrite.
- **Motion-graphics B-roll:** zero.
- **Color grade:** zero.
- **Cutting:** no filler or in-clip retake cutting.
- **Spanish:** broken (`--language en`, English GLUE list).
- **In-app AI:** Gemini-only.
- **Manual polish:** the UI can't retime captions or B-roll.

Remotion's Company License applies above 3 employees.

Net: a reasonable fork base, or better a donor of mcp/server.mjs plus the anchoring model plus the transcription and B-roll scripts, if the user commits to Remotion. It is no head start on captions or motion graphics. Lowered from 6 to 5 after the UI and MCP-contract findings.

Spanish accent-matching risk overstated: norm() is /[^a-z0-9%$]/gi and is applied to both sides of the comparison, so stripping á/é/ñ rarely breaks matching. The real Spanish blockers are `--language en`, the English initial_prompt and the English-only GLUE list.

license_risks:
The repo's own code is MIT, which is clean to fork. The real exposure is Remotion, which the preview and render path cannot do without.

Packages under the Remotion License ('SEE LICENSE IN LICENSE.md' or 'Remotion License', v4.0.380):
- remotion, @remotion/player, @remotion/cli (direct deps)
- @remotion/renderer, @remotion/bundler (transitive)
- @remotion/install-whisper-cpp, @remotion/media-parser (direct but unused)

The @remotion/compositor-* native binaries have no license field; they come from the same Remotion project and fall under its terms. @remotion/web-renderer (transitive via studio) is marked UNLICENSED. @remotion/studio, captions, media-utils, licensing and streaming are MIT.

The Remotion License (remotion-dev/remotion LICENSE.md, verified):
- Free for individuals, for-profit organizations of up to 3 employees, non-profits, and evaluation.
- Otherwise a paid Company License is required (remotion.pro).
- Copying or modifying Remotion itself to sell your own derivative of Remotion is disallowed.
- A license change is announced for Remotion 5.0.
A commercial product built on this fork carries the same obligation once the company passes 3 employees.

Other components:
- **WhisperX:** BSD-2. The Whisper weights are MIT.
- **pyannote:** WhisperX's pyannote-based diarization/VAD models are gated on Hugging Face under their own terms. This repo passes --vad_onset and --vad_offset and doesn't enable diarization; check which VAD backend the installed WhisperX version uses.
- **Pexels:** content is under the Pexels License (free, no attribution required, some resale and redistribution limits). The repo doesn't track sources.

stack:
A TypeScript monorepo with npm workspaces:
- UI: SolidJS + Vite in an Electron ^43.1.1 shell.
- Runtime: a headless ECS on koota 0.6.6, patched via patch-package (patches/koota+0.6.6.patch). It draws with Canvas2D and uses WebGPU for shaderPaint.
- Projects: SolidJS JSX files, reconciled onto the ECS. UI edits are written back to the source with ts-morph.
- Encoding: mediabunny (MPL-2.0) over WebCodecs.
- Motion: anime.js 4 plus Chromium's experimental html-in-canvas (drawElementImage, turned on by the CanvasDrawElement blink flag in apps/desktop/src/main.ts:74).
- Agent side: @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk, `codex app-server` over stdio JSON-RPC, and an MCP server on @modelcontextprotocol/sdk (Streamable HTTP on loopback).
- Cloud: a closed tRPC backend at api.diffusion.studio (@diffusionstudio/api-contract holds only types), with optional Supabase auth, Umami analytics and the @sentry/solid SDK.

summary:
This is a new MPL-2.0 Electron editor built around 'compositions as code'. A project is a folder of SolidJS JSX. Claude Code or Codex edits those files, and a local MCP server plus a matching `diffusion` CLI give the agent perception and verification tools: probe, grab, filmstrip, waveform with silence ranges, transcribe, listen, capture, check, export.

The LLM harness is real and is the standout part:
- packages/agent-chat/src/host/claude.ts drives the user's own `claude` binary through the Agent SDK.
- codex.ts runs `codex app-server` over JSON-RPC.
- Both are wired in as the default harnesses (host/index.ts:54).
- apps/desktop/src/mcp-config.ts registers the MCP server in 9 agent configs.
This is very close to the architecture the user described.

On the user's specific question, whether it has premium captions like Captions.ai: it does not. It has the same gap as autobroll.
- It ships 7 hard-coded presets in packages/runtime/src/media/caption/.
- The best of them colors the active word (spotlight), or enlarges and recolors the active half-line (guinea).
- Nothing gives per-word pop, bounce or scale, emoji, or LLM/keyword emphasis.
- The only word-level motion is appearWord/appearChar/scramble text reveals on the whole node.

Other gaps:
- Cutting: a crude peak-threshold silence detector plus LLM judgment guided by a markdown walkthrough. There is no filler or retake algorithm, even though the README says 'Removes filler words'.
- Color: 7 CSS-filter color effects (brightness, contrast, grayscale, hue rotation, invert, saturate, sepia) or shaders the LLM writes in WGSL.
- Motion graphics: whatever the LLM writes (html-in-canvas driven by anime.js, WebGPU). There are zero animated templates and no SFX.
- Stock footage: no stock search.
- Backend: auto-transcription, listen and generate.* upload media to Diffusion Studio's closed, credit-metered backend.
captions_detail:
Files re-read:
- packages/runtime/src/media/caption/{index,types,utils,position,subtitles,classic,cascade,spotlight,whisper,paper,guinea,stark}.ts
- packages/runtime/src/utils/text-motion.ts
- packages/runtime/src/constants.ts (CaptionType has exactly 7 values)
- docs/reference/jsx/captions.md, docs/reference/jsx/animations.md
- apps/web/src/dapi/handlers/media-transcribe.ts

What the 7 presets actually do in code:
- classic: groupBy duration 0.2 s (1-2 words at a time), Urbanist, drop shadow.
- whisper: 2 s phrases, Montserrat.
- cascade: up to 50 chars; words appear once started. No per-word animation.
- spotlight: up to 10 chars; a TextRange recolors the active word to #24D5FF.
- paper: two lines; the active line gets fontWeight 500.
- guinea: uppercase 'The Bold Font'; the active HALF-GROUP line is 1.1x size, with the color picked from a fixed PSEUDO_RANDOM_SEQUENCE of 3 colors. captions.md says 'the spoken word enlarges', but the code enlarges the line, so the doc overstates it.
- stark: Figtree with a DIFFERENCE blend.

Props are limited to colors[], verticalAlign (top/center/bottom, anchored to a fixed 100 px margin in position.ts), offsetX/Y, and timing trims. text-motion.ts only implements revealWords/revealChars/scramble, which act on the whole node's text string.

Missing: per-word scale/pop/bounce keyframes, emoji, keyword or LLM emphasis, per-word background boxes, face-aware placement, and a word-editing UX.

Transcription: trpc.transcribe.mutate uploads the transcoded audio to api.diffusion.studio. No language parameter is sent, so Spanish quality is unknown. Bring-your-own transcripts are possible:
- A .json transcript keeps real word timings.
- .srt/.vtt go through subtitles.ts, which SYNTHESIZES word timings in proportion to word length within each cue. That makes karaoke-style highlights inaccurate unless you supply word-level JSON (for example from a local WhisperX).

A realistic route to premium captions here would be new CaptionDecoder classes, or LLM-authored <html> + anime.js caption overlays driven by the word JSON. Neither exists today.

The only way to get motion graphics is for the LLM to write the code. Verified paths:
1. <html>: packages/runtime/src/media/html.ts checks for 'drawElementImage' on CanvasRenderingContext2D, which needs the CanvasDrawElement flag set in apps/desktop/src/main.ts:74. It is driven by a paused anime.js timeline seeked from the playhead (docs/examples/05-anime-timeline.tsx).
2. <shaderPaint> WGSL (packages/runtime/src/media/shader.ts) and <surface> for three.js/WebGPU (examples 06-10).
3. <adjustmentLayer> with keyframed scale for punch-in zooms (docs/reference/jsx/adjustment-layer.md).
4. In/out presets: fade, slide x4, grow, shrink, spin, twist, blur.

Templates and assets:
- docs/brand/assets/components/{callout,lower-third,title-card,media-grid}.tsx are static <rect>+<text> with no <animation>, keyframes or anime usage (grep confirms).
- docs/brand/assets/audio/sfx holds only a .gitkeep.
- There are no icon, stat-counter or UI-mockup packs.
- diffusionstudio/open-projects (121 stars) has about 4 worked example projects.

html.md documents rasterizer bugs: CSS scale() on large or clipped subtrees blanks them, and fractional opacity on painted boxes drops the subtree mid-fade. Scale-based text pops inside <html> are therefore fragile. The authoring surface is powerful, but it is an empty canvas plus docs, not a motion library.

summary:
The repo is real, and most of the architecture claims hold up when checked against the code. It is an offline, Korean-first, macOS-first Electron editor:
- whisper.cpp word timings drive text-based cuts through a zod-validated EditCommand bus with 17 verbs, dry-run, state invariants and an audit log. The audit log is hash-chained but uses the non-cryptographic cyrb53 hash.
- Silences can be found with ffmpeg silencedetect or from transcript gaps. Filler removal is an exact-match lexicon lookup.
- Color is 6 eq/curves presets plus signalstats auto-enhance.
- Reframe is a center crop to 9:16 or 1:1.
- A local Qwen2.5-1.5B planner has a regex fallback.
- A stdio MCP server exposes open, manifest, plan, dry_run, apply, save, audit, find_words, find_silences and render.

Captions are not premium. They are 12 static Canvas2D presets. "Animation" means swapping whole-cue PNG sub-frames (reveal, karaoke recolor, typewriter) or scaling the whole cue in ("pop"). There is no per-word transform, glow, shadow or emoji. Keyword emphasis is a longest-word heuristic with a Korean stopword list.

Motion graphics are 12 low-res procedural GIF stickers (several bake in Apple Color Emoji glyphs), a keyframed ffmpeg overlay engine and a zoompan punch-in. No UI control or render test exercises the punch-in, and it very likely breaks on non-720p footage. There is no stock search. The 6 b-roll loops are not wired into the app.

Re-verification also found problems the first pass missed:
1. The renderer is single-source: every segment reads input 0 and a project has one mediaPath, so several clips or takes cannot be assembled.
2. Video overlays are not time-shifted, so b-roll placed after t=0 plays from the wrong offset.
3. MCP save_project drops v3 project state (overlays, BGM, manual cues, TTS, glossary, reframe) and overwrites the opened .dawn by default.
4. MCP render ignores the project's overlays, BGM and manual cues.
5. The GUI never passes Spanish to whisper. It retries only in Korean.

It is a decent donor of patterns (command bus, selectors, dry-run/audit, MCP session) but a weak base for premium captions, motion-graphics b-roll, or es/en creators.
captions_detail:
Files read: packages/core/src/subtitles.ts, burn.ts, draw.ts, keywords.ts, templates.ts, caption.ts; apps/mcp/src/session.ts.
- Cues: transcriptToCues groups live words and splits on program gap (default 600 ms), max words (8), max chars and sentence-ending punctuation. Each cue keeps per-word program timings (CueWord). When animation is on, cueOptsForAnim forces at most 4 words, 13 chars and a 400 ms gap.
- Animation: captionFrames expands one cue into static sub-frames. 'reveal' accumulates words. 'karaoke' shows the full text with the active word passed as the emphasis color. 'typewriter' accumulates characters, capped at 24 frames. 'pop' is one frame plus an overlay scale keyframe (0.6x to 1.0 over the first 22% of the cue, easeOut) applied to the whole caption PNG.
  - Every sub-frame is drawn by drawSubtitle into its own 1000x150 PNG and composited as a separate ffmpeg overlay input with -loop 1 -t total.
  - There is no per-word transform (scale, bounce, rotation), no per-word entrance or exit, no glow, drop shadow, gradient or motion blur.
- Styles: 12 SUBTITLE_PRESETS (default, tiktok, podcast, cinematic, highlight, korean, koreanShorts, youtubeBold, varietyYellow, neon, minimal, captionBar). They only vary fill, a text-hugging rounded background, stroke, font family/weight/scale and emphasisColor. The code comment says "neon" is not a real glow.
- Six STYLE_PACKS bundle a caption style, a color preset and removeFillers as EditCommand[].
- Emphasis: pickKeywords is language-agnostic but naive. It ranks by glyph length after dropping Korean stopwords and picks at most 2 words per cue. On English or Spanish text it runs, but it just highlights the longest words. There is no LLM or sentiment input, and the custom-stopwords option is not reachable from the burn path (emphasisCores calls it without options).
- Emoji: drawEmoji is used only for stickers. Captions never get emoji.
- Placement: one global x/y/scale (default 0.1/0.8/0.8), optional per-cue position for manual cues, wrap at 16 chars and 2 lines.
- Fonts are system fonts (Apple SD Gothic Neo, Pretendard, Noto CJK, Impact) and none are bundled.
- Verdict: about 2/5. Basic working animated subtitles at roughly CapCut-basic level, clearly below Submagic/Captions.ai. It does not solve the user's premium-captions problem any better than AutoBroll does.
motion_graphics_detail:
All of it is template or procedural. The LLM writes no motion code.
1) Stickers: scripts/make-gif-stickers.ts draws 12 stickers at 192 px, 12 frames, 12 fps: spinner, pulse fire/star, float-heart, bounce tada/thumbs-up, slide-arrow, blink-new, heart-burst, check-pop, a zoom-subscribe click story and a wave. Most draw Apple Color Emoji glyphs, so the bundled GIFs redistribute Apple emoji artwork. There are also 2 ProRes 4444 alpha MOVs, but the app only lists .gif files (main 'assets:motionStickers'), so the MOVs are never used in the app. The UI also has 12 static emoji stickers rasterized at runtime.
2) B-roll pack: scripts/make-broll-pack.ts makes 6 abstract 1080x1920 loops (assets/broll). Nothing in packages/, apps/ or sidecar/ references them and they are not in extraResources, so they are not wired in.
3) Overlay engine (packages/core/src/overlay.ts, easing.ts):
   - Real and tested (g14, g19, g21, g22, g26): keyframed x/y/scale via ffmpeg expressions with linear, easeIn, easeOut, easeInOut and back-overshoot easing, plus opacity, static rotation, blend modes and enable= time gating.
   - Defect: video and MOV overlay inputs get no setpts or itsoffset. A clip placed at t0 > 0 therefore shows the frame at program time t (or loops or freezes), not its own first frame. The g23 test uses a solid-color clip, so it cannot catch this.
4) Zoom punch (effects.ts zoomFilter, applyZoom verb):
   - Only center, linear from→to.
   - The code omits zoompan's `s` option, assuming the input size is kept. ffmpeg's default is hd720, so on 1080x1920 footage the zoomed segments come out 1280x720, which breaks the concat or crop.
   - No integration or demo test renders a zoom, the UI has no zoom control (the verb only appears as a label), and it is not in PLANNER_VERBS.
5) Promo templates: scripts/lib-promo-templates.ts has 3 image-promo layouts. They exist only as scripts, and the OpenRouter LLM only picks a template id and copy.
6) Transitions: xfade fade and dip-to-black.
Missing: kinetic typography, animated stats/counters, icons, lower thirds, UI mockups, SFX, and any Remotion, Lottie, GSAP or HTML engine. Score 2, at the low end: the engine is basic and working, but the visual library is toy-level.
llm_integration_detail:
(a) Local planner: sidecar/llm (chat.ts, index.ts, server.ts).
- It spawns llama.cpp llama-server or llama-cli with Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct Q4_K_M and a GBNF grammar (core/grammar.ts). core/planner.ts builds a Korean prompt with few-shot examples and a PLANNER_VERBS whitelist of 10 verbs; parsePlan and dryRunCommands validate the result.
- rule-planner.ts is the regex fallback.
- The core depends only on `type PlanProvider = (prompt: string) => Promise<string>` (planner.ts:32), so another backend is trivial to plug in. DAWN_LLAMA_SERVER_URL can point at any llama-server.

(b) MCP: apps/mcp/src/index.ts (stdio) with 11 tools in mcp-server.ts. command_manifest returns all 17 EditCommand verbs, so an external agent is not limited to the planner's 10. session.ts reuses applyCommand, dryRunCommands, appendAudit/verifyAudit and subtitleBurnPlan, and rasterizes captions with @napi-rs/canvas. So Claude Code or Codex can drive cut, style and color edits today via `npx tsx apps/mcp/src/index.ts`. The bin is a raw .ts file and needs a built @dawn-cut/core; the package is not published.
Verified gaps:
1. No ingest or transcribe tool. A .dawn project must first be created in the GUI.
2. No tool that returns the transcript text (state_summary gives counts only). The agent has to read the .dawn JSON itself to spot retakes.
3. session.save() calls makeProject with only subtitleStyle and subtitlePos. Saving a v3 project drops overlays, manualCues, ttsClips, reframe, colorPreset, autoEnhanceEq, glossary and bgm, and by default it overwrites the opened file (data loss).
4. session.render() passes only burned subtitle overlays. It ignores project overlays, stickers, BGM, manual cues and the project's saved reframe, even though issue #1, which claimed overlay burn-in, is closed.
5. Tool descriptions and the plan prompt are in Korean.

(c) Cloud: scripts/demo-cloud-planner.ts and scripts/promo-agent.ts make hard-coded fetch calls to OpenRouter (promo-agent defaults to model anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6), reading the key from ~/Library/Application Support/Electron/settings.json. sidecar/tts/cloud.ts calls OpenRouter, ElevenLabs and OpenAI TTS. None of this is a provider abstraction.

There are no Claude Code skills and no Codex-specific integration. Score lowered to 2: the MCP path works for a subset of edits, but it cannot do a full edit end to end and it can lose project state.
license_risks:
Low for code, but the first pass missed two asset/packaging items.
Code and binaries:
- The code is MIT.
- FFmpeg runs as a subprocess. The packaged build is n7.1, static, --disable-gpl --disable-nonfree (scripts/build-ffmpeg-lgpl.sh). It has no libx264 and encodes with h264_videotoolbox, so the packaged encoder is macOS-only. Shipping a static LGPL binary inside the DMG still brings LGPL source-availability obligations; NOTICE only links ffmpeg.org. The dev setup (setup-binaries.sh) uses Homebrew's GPL ffmpeg with libx264, and detectH264Encoder prefers libx264 when it is present. On Linux or Windows you would need libx264 (GPL, which makes distribution a GPL question) or another encoder.
- whisper.cpp (MIT, statically built) with ggml-large-v3-turbo downloaded at runtime (Whisper weights are MIT). llama.cpp (MIT). Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct (Apache-2.0, user-downloaded; the 3B variant is deliberately avoided). @napi-rs/canvas (MIT). lucide-react (ISC).
- No Remotion (so no company-license threshold exposure), no GSAP, no Lottie.
Missed by the first pass:
- Bundled sticker assets (assets/gif/*.gif and thumbs-up.mov / zoom-subscribe.mov) are made by scripts/make-gif-stickers.ts, which draws "Apple Color Emoji" glyphs (fire, star, heart, tada, thumbs-up, check, bell, pointing hand, wave, arrow). Those are Apple-copyrighted images and are not licensed for redistribution. NOTICE describes the assets as self-generated. Do not reuse these assets.
- Optional scripts/setup-tts-neural.sh downloads Piper binaries (they link espeak-ng, which is GPL-3) and the en_US-lessac-medium voice (dataset terms are research-oriented). These are user-downloaded, not bundled.
Other:
- BGM and b-roll loops are procedurally generated by the author's scripts.
- Demo photos come from picsum.photos under the Unsplash License and are test fixtures only.
- Optional cloud APIs (OpenRouter, ElevenLabs, OpenAI) are under their own terms.
- Caption fonts are system fonts and are not bundled.

fit_rationale:
The architectural ideas match the user's harness concept:
- A zod-validated EditCommand bus with dry-run, invariants and an audit log.
- Word-level transcript to EDL.
- Read-only NL selectors (findWords, findSilences), so the LLM never computes microseconds.
- An MCP server that lets Claude Code or Codex act as the brain.
Those are worth copying.

As a fork base it is weaker than the first pass suggested:
- The renderer and project model are single-source, so multiple takes or clips cannot be assembled.
- The MCP path can drop project state on save, and its render ignores overlays and BGM.
- Zoom punch-ins and time-offset b-roll overlays are likely broken.
- Captions are PNG frame swaps with no per-word motion.
- The motion-graphics library is 12 tiny emoji GIFs, which carry an Apple-emoji licensing problem.
- Filler, keyword and transcription-language handling is Korean-first, with no Spanish path in the GUI.
- Retake detection and stock b-roll are absent.
- Packaging is macOS-only, the UI is a 4,750-line monolith, and there is one maintainer who has gone quiet.

The two things the user cares about most, premium captions and motion-graphics b-roll, would have to be rebuilt on a real motion engine (Remotion, HTML/Canvas or Lottie). Best used as a donor of patterns and small pure modules, not forked whole.

reusable_parts.part: EditCommand bus: zod schemas, reducer, JSON-Schema manifest, dry-run, invariant gate
reusable_parts.use_for: A validated verb layer that Claude Code or Codex calls via MCP, with preview-before-apply and granular errors the agent can self-correct from

reusable_parts.part: Hash-chained audit log (cyrb53, non-cryptographic)
reusable_parts.use_for: A replayable edit history and tamper detection for agent edits. Not a security signature.

reusable_parts.part: MCP server over stdio wrapping an editing session
reusable_parts.use_for: A template for exposing tools to Claude Code or Codex (open, manifest, dry_run, apply, render, find_words, find_silences). Fix save() to keep all project fields, and add ingest and transcript-read tools, before relying on it.

reusable_parts.part: Word-level transcript to timeline/EDL with program/source time sync
reusable_parts.use_for: Text-based cutting and mapping word timings into program time for captions. It must be extended for multi-source EDLs.

reusable_parts.part: whisper.cpp full-JSON token merge to word timestamps
reusable_parts.use_for: Local word-level STT (-ojf, merging BPE leading-space tokens). The sidecar accepts `lang` (-l es/en), but the GUI never passes it, so always pass it explicitly.

reusable_parts.part: NL selectors findWords / findSilences
reusable_parts.use_for: Letting the LLM point at phrases and gaps by wordId instead of computing microseconds. A natural base for LLM-driven retake removal.

reusable_parts.part: ffmpeg renderEdl filter_complex pieces (trim/concat, xfade fold, atempo, BGM sidechaincompress ducking, encoder detection)
reusable_parts.use_for: Reference snippets for a final-assembly step. Do not reuse as-is: single-source input, and zoompan with no s= option.

reusable_parts.part: Keyframed overlay expression builder with easing, including back-overshoot
reusable_parts.use_for: Compositing pre-rendered alpha motion-graphic clips onto the base video. Add setpts=PTS-STARTPTS+T0/TB (or itsoffset) for video inputs first, or clips play from the wrong offset.

reusable_parts.part: Color presets plus signalstats auto-enhance
reusable_parts.use_for: A cheap one-tap exposure/contrast/saturation fix and preset looks

reusable_parts.part: Silence detection via ffmpeg silencedetect
reusable_parts.use_for: Silence cutting independent of STT

reusable_parts.part: Caption cue chunking and word sub-frame timing
reusable_parts.use_for: Cue grouping by max words, chars, gap and sentence end, to feed a real per-word animation renderer. The Canvas2D PNG rendering itself is not worth reusing.

red_flags: Captions are not premium: static Canvas2D presets with frame-swap reveal, karaoke recolor, typewriter and whole-cue pop. No per-word motion, glow, shadow or emoji; emphasis is a longest-word heuristic.
Renderer and project are single-source (renderEdl reads only segments[0].mediaPath via [0:v]/[0:a]; the store has one mediaPath). Multiple clips or takes cannot be combined.

summary: The previous evaluation holds up closely against the code. Tscaps is an open-core, in-browser caption editor positioned as a Submagic alternative. Confirmed: there are 38 templates in 5 categories (classic, modern, viral, key-moments, lab), and each is real SCSS driven by per-word, line and segment timing CSS variables. There are 15 animation primitives, each with a controls.json. Emoji decorations have their own timing variables. Words carry semanticTags and tag CSS classes. The rendering is deterministic, frozen-frame CSS. The README states outright that the LLM tagging runs only on the hosted tscaps.io; the open-source catalog has only the regex Number and Quote taggers (ClientTaggerCatalog.ts), and the blank lines in bootstrap/wiring/tagging.ts show where remote taggers were removed. Auto-cut removes silences only, found from gaps between Whisper word timestamps. BadTakeFinder needs a 'cut' tag, and RemoveBadTakesAction has no UI caller (code search finds it only in wiring and in its own file). There is no color grade, B-roll, motion graphics, SFX or LLM harness. I found five factual errors or omissions. (1) The engine CLI example (examples/cli/runner.ts) renders only with defaults: withInputVideo plus built-in Whisper, with no Document, CSS or skipRanges passed. RenderPipelineBuilder has no skipRanges method, so cuts need MediaBunnyVideoRenderer and RenderJob called directly. (2) The template HTML/DOM builder (rendering/subtitle/SegmentSubtreeHtmlBuilder.ts, 406 lines, MIT) is not exported from the engine. Porting the templates into Remotion therefore means copying or rewriting it plus the baseline CSS, not just emitting classes and variables. (3) Three key-moments templates (luca, luna, milo) require the video frame inside the caption DOM (rendering.videoFrame.required) and use mix-blend-mode, and pastor requires behindActor (MediaPipe, AGPL studio). (4) The Loki template depends on the Komika Axis font. Its freeware license forbids selling the font and forbids modifying it for repackaging or re-release, and the font file lives in the AGPL studio directory. (5) The committed examples/output/cli-defaults.mp4 contains avc1/avcC and mp4a boxes. That is some evidence the headless Playwright path has produced H.264 at least once, on an unknown OS. For the user's question ('autobroll has captions, but not premium ones like Captions.ai'), this is still the best donor for the caption styling layer: the MIT templates, the animation library, the timing-variable contract and the tag and emoji model. The automatic part (which words to emphasize, which emoji, which hook) must come from your own Claude Code or Codex step. It is a poor base to fork for the whole product.

scores.evidence: Read apps/studio/src/core/cuts/services/SilenceFinder.ts. It walks the segments and words and emits gaps between word.time.end and the next word.time.start that exceed a threshold. There is one threshold for gaps inside a segment and one for gaps at segment edges; the code calls these 'isInterSentence', but they are segment boundaries, not real sentences. SilencePadder pads the gaps. apps/studio/src/core/cuts/domain/RemoveSilencesPreset.ts has natural 0.6/1.2 s, fast 0.4/0.7 s and faster 0.2/0.4 s. packages/engine/src/modules/video/RenderJob.ts has skipRanges, and RenderTimeMap.ts has a test. BadTakeFinder.ts only merges runs of words tagged 'cut', padded by up to 0.08 s. apps/studio/src/ui/.../timeline/components/CutsMenuScreen.tsx has only 'Remove silences' and 'Restore all cuts'. gh code search for removeBadTakes finds only wiring/cuts.ts and RemoveBadTakesAction.ts.
scores.notes: This is a basic but working silence cutter. It does not use audio energy or VAD (a MediaBunnyWaveformExtractor exists, but it feeds the timeline waveform display, not the silence finder), and it has no filler-word list and no retake detection. All of this cut logic is AGPL except RenderTimeMap and skipRanges.

scores.evidence: packages/engine/src/modules/video/mediabunny/frame/LayeredFrameCompositor.ts only calls frame.draw, then overlay.draw, captions.draw and topLayer.draw, with no filter, LUT or shader. The tree has no grade or LUT code. The SVG filters in templates/_lib/filters/recipes are outline, drop-shadow and chromatic-split for caption text.

I read templates/naya/style.scss: Anton uppercase, the SVG #hype-outline filter, a segment rise-in and a word pop-in on --on-word-being-narrated-starts, a yellow .word-being-narrated, and emojis above or below the segment with an angle-based spring entry keyframe. templates/enzo/style.scss makes .emphasis/.accent/.entity scale 1.4x with a glow and makes .emphasis/.entity EB Garamond italic. templates/levi/style.scss is a gradient background-clip hook with a line rise-in. templates/milo/style.scss uses container style queries for big-last-word layouts. templates/_lib/animation has 15 primitives (bob, fade-in, flash-in, glitch-in, highlight-pulse, jitter, pop-in, rise-in, scale-in, settle-in, shimmer, slide-in, snap-in, typewriter, wobble-in), each with a controls.json. packages/engine/src/modules/document/CssVariable.ts defines per-state start, end and duration variables for word, line and segment, plus index, char count and width. Word.ts pushes each semanticTag as a CSS class and holds a Decoration. Decoration.ts gives emoji glyphs their own timing variables. apps/studio/src/core/tagging/domain/TagName.ts has 11 tags. SheetRole.ts sends hook to levi and peak to elio. A python survey of all 38 template.json files found the 5 categories. 13 templates style tag classes and 11 use decorations.
scores.notes: The styling system is pro-grade. It is not a 5 because the open-source build does no automatic emphasis, emoji or hook selection (the README note confirms this), so 13 of the tag-driven templates look plain until someone tags words by hand. There are no caption SFX. I did not visually check render quality, and the README's sample clips were made on the hosted cloud with LLM tags. SmartLowercaseEffect preserves only the English pronoun 'I' and tagged words, so untagged Spanish proper nouns get lowercased.

scores.evidence: The tree has no stock or Pexels code. RenderJob has a single `video: File`, and the only other layers are overlayHtml, captions and topLayer.

No graphics templates exist. BrowserOverlayFrameRenderer.ts (41 lines) rasterizes a static overlayHtml once. The only kinetic typography is inside the caption templates (the key-moments hook and peak styles levi, elio, milo, luca and luna). FrozenFrameCss.ts is a one-line CSS constant (paused plus fill-mode both !important).
scores.notes: This is generous. There are no stats, icons, lower thirds, UI mockups, zoom punches or SFX, and no LLM-authored graphics path. The 1 reflects only the caption-bound kinetic hook text and the reusable frozen-frame and negative-delay idea.

scores.evidence: gh code search finds no matches for openai, anthropic or chat/completions. The 'LLM' hits are README text, SKILL.md and false positives. apps/studio/src/bootstrap/wiring/tagging.ts registers only ClientTaggerCatalog (Number and Quote), with blank lines where remote taggers were. TaggerDescriptor.ts defines the appliedBy modes 'client', 'remote' and 'on-demand'. skills/tscaps-api/SKILL.md documents the paid api.tscaps.io REST API with a bearer key. templates/README.md has a section 'Authoring with an LLM' that tells users to paste AUTHORING.md and _docs into Codex or Claude Code to write new templates.
scores.notes: The engine has no provider lock-in because it has no provider at all. The seams are real: PassthroughTranscriber(document) accepts a pre-built Document with semanticTags and decorations, RenderPipelineBuilder.withCss() and withTranscriber() exist, and the template docs are written for agents to author new styles.

scores.evidence: LayeredFrameCompositor.ts stacks frame, overlay, captions and topLayer. DefaultCodecPolicy.ts uses mediabunny getFirstEncodableVideoCodec, sets bitrate by quality factor and codec efficiency (avc, hevc, vp9, av1, vp8), and throws if no encoder exists. RenderJob supports mp4 and webm, skipRanges, audio passthrough, transcode or discard, and a fallback decoder. The subtitle pipeline (rendering/subtitle/*: BatchPlanner, SpriteSheetCompositor, KeyframeScanAnimationStateFingerprint, SvgFilterMaterializer) batches caption states into sprite sheets. examples/cli/run.ts launches Playwright chromium and a Vite server and saves the download. The committed examples/output/cli-defaults.mp4 (1.7 MB) contains avc1, avcC and mp4a boxes. docs/RENDERING_INTERNALS.md (78 lines) documents the foreignObject differences in Firefox and Safari.
scores.notes: This is a solid caption burn-in renderer, but the scope is narrow: one input video, no multi-clip or B-roll tracks, a static overlay, no alpha-channel caption output and no GPU effects. It is tied to the browser. The CLI example uses only defaults, so custom Document, CSS or cuts need your own runner, and cuts require calling MediaBunnyVideoRenderer and RenderJob directly because the builder has no skipRanges. Speed is not measured.

scores.evidence: The timeline components are real, not stubs: Timeline.tsx (245 lines), Row.tsx (311), Waveform.tsx (82), chips/WordChip.tsx (134) and overlays/CutOverlay.tsx (170), plus SilenceLayer, SceneRunLayer, ScenePopover, SelectionToolbar and ZoomStepper. There are transcript decoration components (EmojiPickerScreen.tsx, EmojiPopover.tsx) and CutsMenuScreen.tsx. CI runs Playwright e2e against the studio.
scores.notes: I sampled file sizes and the cuts menu, not full UX. It is AGPL, and it has no B-roll or overlay tracks.

scores.evidence: There are 153 test files (38 in the engine) and 4 e2e specs. verify.yml runs typecheck, lint, engine and web unit tests, the build and e2e. There are extensive JSDoc and templates/_docs (9 files: css-contract, animation, library, filters, rendering, style-controls, template-json, checklist, README), and engine-publish and docker-publish workflows.
scores.notes: Against that: one author (bus factor 1), 40 commits that are all mirror syncs from a private repo, only 3.5 months of history, pre-1.0, open-core with stripped seams, and heavy abstraction relative to what it does (captions only).

captions_detail: Verified mechanism: each Word, Line and Segment becomes a span or div. Classes include word, the narration-state classes (word-being-narrated and so on), one class per semantic tag, and last-word-in-line. Elements also get CSS variables such as --on-word-being-narrated-starts = (start - currentTime)s, --word-index, --segment-index, char counts and --*-width-em. Decorations (emoji) get their own time variables. FROZEN_FRAME_CSS freezes every animation (play-state paused and fill-mode both, both !important), so a frame is a pure function of the playhead. The templates are real and varied. Naya has an outline filter, Anton uppercase, a word pop-in, a yellow active word and spring-in emoji placed by segment index. Enzo gives tag words a 1.4x EB Garamond italic with a glow. Levi is a gradient-clipped hook line. Milo does big-last-word layouts with container style queries and mix-blend-mode against the video. The build and runtime extras are control variables with fallbacks (var(--control, default)), variants, splitters (balanced pixel width, boundary score, pause-based, speaker change), effects (GapFree, SmartLowercase, SmartPunctuation, RemovePunctuation, CarryQuotes), SRT/VTT/ASS/TTML/SBV/TXT export, RTL/bidi, and text behind the speaker (MediaPipe, AGPL). The gap for 'premium like Captions.ai' is automation: nothing picks emphasis, entity, hook, peak or stat words or emojis in the open-source build. That is exactly the piece Claude Code or Codex should produce as JSON (word index to tags and emoji), and the Document model accepts it directly (Word.semanticTags, Word.decoration, PassthroughTranscriber). Porting caveats the previous evaluation missed: SegmentSubtreeHtmlBuilder (406 lines, MIT) is not exported, so a Remotion port has to copy or reimplement it along with BaselineCssComposer, DecorationContainerBaselineCss and SegmentPaddingCssRuleBuilder. 5 templates also ship filters.svg defs that must be injected. luca, luna and milo need the video frame inside the caption DOM (which is easier in Remotion, where captions sit over the video in one DOM). pastor needs behindActor segmentation. Loki uses the restricted Komika Axis font. Comparison: autobroll's /Users/felipealonzo/autobroll/src/CaptionTrack.tsx (103 lines) has one hard-coded look. It uses Inter, a per-word accent flag (weight 800 plus accent color), scale 1.05 on the active or accent word, and a page fade and slide. So tscaps templates would be a large step up in variety and motion.
motion_graphics_detail: No motion-graphics B-roll exists. There are no stats, icons, lower thirds, UI mockups, zoom punches, SFX, graphics templates or LLM-authored graphics code. BrowserOverlayFrameRenderer paints one static overlayHtml and reuses it on every frame. The only kinetic typography is caption-bound: the key-moments templates (levi, elio, milo, luca, luna, pastor) and the viral ones. The reusable idea is the frozen-frame technique (FROZEN_FRAME_CSS plus negative animation-delay variables computed from the playhead), which renders any HTML/CSS animation deterministically frame by frame. It is a one-line constant, and Remotion users can easily do the same thing themselves.
llm_integration_detail: The open-source build contains no LLM calls: no OpenAI or Anthropic SDK, no prompts and no MCP server (verified by code search). LLM tagging for emphasis, hook, peak, emoji and bad takes runs only in the closed tscaps.io cloud, which the README note states. skills/tscaps-api/SKILL.md (MIT) is a vendor skill that sends media to the paid api.tscaps.io, not a local tool. Plug-in points for a Claude Code or Codex brain: (1) have the agent output word-level JSON (tags, emoji, hook and peak spans, 'cut' spans for bad takes), build an engine Document with semanticTags and Decoration, and pass it through withTranscriber(new PassthroughTranscriber(doc)) and withCss(compiledTemplateCss); (2) for cuts, call MediaBunnyVideoRenderer.render with RenderJob.skipRanges, since the builder does not expose skipRanges; (3) run it headless through a Playwright runner modeled on examples/cli/run.ts (which currently renders defaults only); (4) point an agent at templates/AUTHORING.md and templates/_docs to generate new caption styles, which the repo's templates/README.md explicitly encourages. The alternative is to port the templates into autobroll's Remotion CaptionTrack and keep one render stack.
license_risks: 1) apps/studio is AGPL-3.0 (full text confirmed). SilenceFinder, BadTakeFinder, the template.json loader, the controls and variants resolver, emoji placement, person segmentation, the timeline UI and the Sass build scripts are all AGPL. Re-implement them; do not copy. 2) The MIT templates cannot be compiled with plain sass. _lib/control.scss calls tscaps-control-field, _lib/font-stack.scss calls tscaps-font-stack, and _lib/animation/declared.scss calls tscaps-declared-animation. These are implemented in AGPL apps/studio/scripts/control-field-function.ts (50 lines), font-stack-function.ts (10) and declared-animation-function.ts (37), and they import AGPL resolvers. No compiled style.build.css is committed (0 in the tree). Rewrite about 20 lines of shims yourself: declared-animation can be a no-op, control-field should return var(--id, default), and font-stack should return a font-family var. 3) New finding: templates/loki uses 'Komika Axis' (apps/studio/src/styles/fonts/komika-axis.woff2 and komika-axis_license.txt). Its Apostrophic Labs freeware terms forbid selling the font and forbid modifying or repackaging it without written permission. Replace the font if you ship Loki commercially. 4) mediabunny is MPL-2.0 (file-level copyleft on modified files). @huggingface/transformers and onnxruntime-web are Apache-2.0/MIT. @mediapipe/tasks-vision is Apache-2.0, and its model URLs are in apps/studio/src/core/person-segmentation/infrastructure/PersonSegmenterModelUrls.ts, fetched from Google storage at runtime. 5) The @fontsource fonts are mostly OFL, so keep their notices. 6) There is no Remotion or GSAP dependency, so tscaps adds no Remotion company-license exposure. Porting the templates into autobroll (Remotion 4.0.380) keeps autobroll's existing Remotion license obligations, since Remotion requires a paid company license above its small-company threshold. 7) The GitHub repo-level license is null because licensing is split per directory, so check the path of every file you copy. 8) Using skills/tscaps-api sends user media to a third-party paid service.

red_flags: Open-core: the LLM tagging for emphasis, hook, peak, emoji and bad takes is cloud-only, as the README states. The open-source catalog contains only the NumberTaggerDescriptor and QuoteTaggerDescriptor, so 13 tag-driven templates look plain unless you tag words by hand or with your own LLM step.
The bad-take flow is dead wiring: RemoveBadTakesAction is constructed in bootstrap/wiring/cuts.ts, but no UI calls it (code search), and no tagger emits 'cut'.
Silence detection uses Whisper word-timestamp gaps, not audio energy, and there is no filler or retake detection.
Split license: all the glue (Sass functions, template loader, controls resolver, cut finders, editor) is AGPL-3.0, and only the engine, templates and skills are MIT.
The MIT templates need custom Sass functions that are implemented only in AGPL scripts, and no compiled CSS is committed.
The segment HTML builder the templates depend on is not exported from @tscaps/engine, so a Remotion port means copying or reimplementing about 400 lines plus the baseline CSS.
The Loki template uses the Komika Axis font, whose freeware license bans sale and repackaging.
The CLI example renders defaults only, and RenderPipelineBuilder has no skipRanges. The earlier claim that it takes a Document, CSS and skipRanges was overstated.

Rendering is browser-bound (foreignObject plus WebCodecs), with documented CSS differences in Firefox and Safari. A committed H.264 example output suggests headless Chromium works, but the OS and Linux support are unverified.
Bus factor 1: 40 mirror commits from a private repo, 3.5 months old, pre-1.0.
Large and heavily abstracted (1,903 files) for a caption-only feature set.
Out of scope entirely: B-roll, motion graphics, color grade, SFX, zoom punches, multi-clip timeline, agent harness.
skills/tscaps-api sends media to a paid third-party API.
fit_rationale: As a base to fork, the fit is poor (3/10). It covers one of the four problems, premium caption styling, and even there the automatic layer that makes Captions.ai and Submagic feel premium (choosing emphasis words, emoji and hooks) is missing from the open-source build. Cutting only removes silences, and there is nothing for color, B-roll, motion graphics or an agent harness. Its browser and WebCodecs render architecture differs from autobroll's Remotion setup, and the editor you would inherit is AGPL and very large. As a donor for the user's exact complaint, it is excellent. Take the MIT templates, the animation primitives, the CSS-variable and class contract, the segment DOM builder, the baseline CSS and the frozen-frame technique. Port them into autobroll's CaptionTrack.tsx, which today has one Inter style with an accent flag and a 1.05 scale. Write your own roughly 20-line Sass shims so everything stays MIT, and have Claude Code or Codex emit per-word tags, emoji and hook and peak spans as JSON. The fallback is a separate headless tscaps burn-in pass built on MediaBunnyVideoRenderer with a PassthroughTranscriber Document. That costs an extra decode and encode and a second render stack, and you would have to write the runner yourself because the example uses defaults only.
corrections: The engine CLI example (examples/cli/runner.ts) only calls new RenderPipelineBuilder().withInputVideo(blob).build() with the built-in Whisper and default style. It does not take a Document, compiled CSS or skipRanges. RenderPipelineBuilder has no skipRanges method; cuts need RenderJob.skipRanges through MediaBunnyVideoRenderer directly (code search finds skipRanges only in RenderJob, MediaBunnyVideoRenderer, subtitle-file and studio export).

Porting the templates into Remotion takes more than emitting classes and variables. SegmentSubtreeHtmlBuilder.ts (406 lines, MIT) builds the required markup (decoration containers above and below, letters, the video-frame layer), and it is not exported from rendering/index.ts. BaselineCssComposer and the decoration baseline CSS also have to come along. I added this as a reusable part and a red flag.

New finding: luca, luna and milo declare rendering.videoFrame.required (the video frame goes inside the caption DOM for mix-blend-mode), and pastor declares behindActor.required (MediaPipe segmentation, AGPL studio). Not every template is a pure overlay.
New license risk: templates/loki uses the Komika Axis font, and its bundled license (apps/studio/src/styles/fonts/komika-axis_license.txt) forbids selling it or modifying it for repackaging.

Custom Sass functions quantified: control-field-function.ts is 50 lines, font-stack-function.ts 10 and declared-animation-function.ts 37 (97 in total, AGPL). control-field returns var(--control, fallback), so a shim that returns the default keeps the templates working.
SilenceFinder's 'inter-sentence' threshold applies to gaps at segment (caption block) edges, not detected sentences.

Answered the question the previous evaluation left open: SmartLowercaseEffect is language-agnostic except that it preserves the English pronoun 'I'. Spanish proper nouns get lowercased unless they are tagged (e.g. entity), which again depends on tagging.
Headless H.264 uncertainty reduced: the committed examples/output/cli-defaults.mp4 contains avc1, avcC and mp4a boxes, so the Playwright path has produced H.264/AAC at least once (OS unknown).

Added an llm_harness seam the previous evaluation missed: templates/README.md has an 'Authoring with an LLM' section that points Codex or Claude Code at AUTHORING.md and _docs to generate templates. The score stays 1 because it is docs, not an integration.

Minor correction on autobroll: CaptionTrack.tsx already has a per-word accent flag (weight 800 plus accent color) and a per-page scale and topPct, not only an active-word 1.05 scale. It is still a single hard-coded look.

All reusable_parts paths the previous evaluation cited exist in the tree (29 checked). The counts of 38 templates, 15 animation primitives, 11 tag names and 153 test files are confirmed. All scores are unchanged; motion_graphics_broll=1 is noted as generous.

license: MIT (LICENSE: Copyright (c) 2026 Junseo5; src-tauri/Cargo.toml license = "MIT"; GitHub spdx MIT). The root package.json is "private": true with no license field.
stack: Tauri 2 desktop app. Rust core (src-tauri/src/core), a small crates/openreelio-core, and a headless Rust CLI (crates/openreelio-cli) with a stdio MCP server, published via npm. Frontend is React 18, TypeScript, Zustand and Tailwind. Rendering is an FFmpeg filter_complex with libass burn-in. Transcription uses whisper-rs (whisper.cpp with DTW); it is in the DEFAULT Cargo features, not opt-in. Also wasmtime 36, webrtc-vad and SQLite, plus an optional Meilisearch. There is no Remotion, no GSAP, no Lottie and no headless browser; Playwright is only used for e2e tests.
size_note: Checked against the git tree: 326 .rs files (13.86 MB) and 1,195 .ts/.tsx files (13.32 MB), 479 of which are *.test.ts[x]. There are 1,595 Fluent emoji PNGs and 12 bundled TTFs. export.rs is 1,025,140 bytes and 26,386 lines, with 377 #[test] and about 4,473 comment lines. mcp.rs is 326 KB, openreelioCodexTools.ts is 207 KB and the CLI integration.rs is 534 KB. Contributors: Junseo5 has 2,103 commits, dependabot 11 and one other person 1. The repo was created 2026-01-10. That volume and the essay-length comments strongly suggest mass AI-generated code.
summary: The repo is real and most of the earlier evaluation holds up. Its strongest part is the LLM harness. Claude Code runs headless (`claude -p`, stream-json in and out, `--tools ""`, `--allowedTools mcp__openreelio__*`, `--strict-mcp-config`, isolated CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR). Codex runs as `codex app-server` in a read-only sandbox with on-request approval. The user picks which one is the brain. One correction: the two brains do not share an MCP surface in the way the earlier evaluation implied. Claude talks to an in-process loopback HTTP MCP server (ipc/commands/openreelio_mcp.rs). Codex has MCP explicitly disabled (`mcp_servers={}`) and gets the same catalog as app-server `dynamicTools`. Both route to one TS executor with about 27 tools, stock search and import included. The standalone `openreelio-cli mcp --stdio` server is a separate Rust implementation with 19 tools and no stock search. The render backbone (gbrap compositing, per-frame keyframed transforms, GPU encoders, contact sheets, QC) is real. It fails the user's main creative goals. Captions are static ASS subtitles: the code comment says \move, \t and \k are 'not emitted here today', ASS braces are escaped so the LLM cannot inject animation, and the DTW word timings are thrown away when captions are created (to_caption). Motion-graphics templates are dead code. Cutting is basic: silence detection and filler removal work, but only in the desktop UI. They use word times estimated by splitting each segment evenly, the filler list is English-only, and the external Claude/Codex brains cannot call them. On the user's AutoBroll question: this repo also has captions that are not premium, and they are even more basic than a 'highlight one word' style.

scores.evidence: src-tauri/src/ipc/commands/transcript_editing.rs: detect_silence_regions runs FFmpeg silencedetect through AudioProfiler, with a cached-bundle fallback. detect_filler_words uses cleanup::DEFAULT_FILLER_WORDS_EN (19 words including 'like', 'so', 'right', 'well', 'actually'). remove_detected_regions applies SplitClipCommand + RippleDeleteCommand in reverse order. The word times come from get_transcript_words, which always returns estimate_word_timings() (annotations/models.rs L291: segment duration / word count). The UI is wired through src/components/features/transcript/CleanupControls.tsx and src/hooks/useCleanupDetection.ts. The CLI has `analysis silence` (crates/openreelio-cli/src/commands/analysis.rs).
scores.notes: Basic but working, and only in the desktop UI. The external brain tool list (OPENREELIO_CODEX_DYNAMIC_TOOLS, shared by the in-app Claude/Codex) and the CLI MCP list have no silence, filler or word-timing tool, so an LLM brain would have to cut from segment-level transcripts with plan_apply. There is no retake or bad-take detection and no Spanish filler list. Filler cuts land at estimated positions rather than on the actual audio.

captions_detail: Generation: whisper.cpp through whisper-rs, a default feature with language auto-detect, so Spanish works with multilingual models. DTW alignment presets cover tiny through large-v3-turbo, followed by a repair pass (MIN_WORD_DURATION_SEC 0.04, energy-onset snapping). Cues are split at 64 chars (24 for CJK) or 6 s. to_caption() discards the word timings, and the Caption model has no word fields. Styling: CaptionStyle has font, size, weight, colour, background, outline, shadow, alignment, italic and underline, plus 8 static packs. Render: one ASS Dialogue per clip with a fixed tag block. \move, \t and \k are never emitted (the code comment says so), and user text is brace-escaped, so an LLM cannot hand-author karaoke or animation tags. Emoji: authored emoji become colour Fluent PNG overlays at libass-measured cells; nothing inserts emoji automatically. QC covers safe area, contrast and extent. Verdict against Captions.ai/Submagic: no per-word animation, highlight, emphasis, auto-emoji, short chunking or animated presets. A premium engine would have to be built. Worth reusing: the DTW word timing, the fonts, the emoji-overlay technique and the caption QC.
motion_graphics_detail: In practice there are none. template/motion_graphics.rs (6 static templates) and core/shapes are unreferenced dead code; the TS types in src/types/templates.ts have no importers found. There are 22 static libass text presets. The only animation that renders is clip transform keyframes (scale and position per frame, zoompan, Ken Burns), which can be used to hand-author zoom punches. The LLM writes no graphics code and there is no HTML, Remotion or Lottie engine. Freesound can supply SFX. Pro-reel motion graphics would need an external engine that renders alpha overlays for the gbrap compositor.
llm_integration_detail: Embedded Claude Code: headless `claude -p` in stream-json with every built-in tool disabled, only mcp__openreelio__* allowed, and a strict MCP config pointing at an in-process loopback HTTP MCP server (openreelio_mcp.rs, bearer token per session). It uses an isolated CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, a pinned official binary downloaded on demand, PTY-based OAuth login (claude_login_pty.rs) and resume. Embedded Codex: `codex app-server` with MCP servers cleared, hooks off, read-only sandbox and on-request approval. Tools are injected as app-server dynamicTools (openreelioCodexTools.ts) and parsed by CodexAppServerClient.ts and CodexNotificationMapper.ts. Both brains share executeOpenReelioAgentToolCall, a catalog of about 27 tools: project and timeline reads, transcription, annotations, clip analysis, semantic_edit_plan, stock search and import, frame_extract, render_proxy, verify, command schema and validate, plan_validate/apply, diff_preview, media_insert and command_execute. Approvals go through approvalBroker.ts and approvalGateway.ts. External harness: `openreelio-cli mcp --stdio`, a separate Rust implementation with 19 tools, read-only by default, with --allow-write or approval tokens. Configs are provided for Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Kimi, Qwen and opencode, along with a Claude plugin with skills and a Codex plugin. Direct providers: Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini and local. Nothing is hard-wired to a single API.
license_risks: OpenReelio's own code is MIT. There is no Remotion or GSAP, so no company-licence exposure. Fonts are OFL-1.1 except Luckiest Guy (Apache-2.0), and the Fluent emoji are MIT, all listed in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md. A real compliance gap: .github/workflows/release.yml runs scripts/prepare-bundled-ffmpeg.mjs, which bundles FFmpeg binaries from scripts/ffmpeg-sources.json (gyan.dev release-essentials, BtbN *-gpl, martin-riedl and evermeet; GPL builds), yet THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md never mentions FFmpeg. Anyone redistributing installers needs to add GPL notices and a source offer. Claude Code is proprietary; OpenReelio does not bundle it and downloads the official binary at runtime, so a fork should keep it that way. Using a user's Claude subscription OAuth inside a third-party app is worth checking against Anthropic's terms. Whisper models are downloaded at runtime. Stock and generative providers (Pexels, Pixabay, Openverse, Freesound, Seedance) each carry their own API terms and per-asset licences, which assets/license_policy.rs tracks.

fit_rationale: The harness is close to what the user wants: Claude headless or Codex app-server, user-selectable, with tool-only access and approvals, plus a CLI MCP and skills. summary:
Re-checked against the code; the prior evaluation mostly holds.

Verified directly:
- agent.ts drives Claude through Agent SDK query() with preset claude_code, settingSources project+user, auto-resume and a final-output gate.
- sceneRender.ts shells out to `hyperframes render -c`.
- Assemble.tsx builds everything from a zod manifest.
- autoTrim.ts sweeps silence thresholds (CANDIDATE_DB -45..-20, WORD_MIDPOINT_MAX_RATE 0.15, 3 TRIM_PROFILES) with a single-pass filter_complex, afade, timestamp remap and residual checks.
- deadWeight.ts is a pure, deterministic detector for filler, stutter, repeat-take (LCS) and hesitation (the speaker's p90), with Vietnamese-only lexicons.
- color.ts has 14 FFmpeg presets, sliders and an HDR tonemap.
- The QC gate is enforced on the server: routes/jobs.ts returns 409 QC_REQUIRED or QC_FAILED for assemble-final. It can be bypassed with force:true or turned off in settings.

On the user's question (autobroll has captions, but not Captions.ai-level): AIEV does not fix this either. CaptionTrack.tsx is one hard-coded karaoke style (cyan active word, 3-frame pop, yellow `hi` keywords, glass pill). It has no presets, no emoji and no varied per-word entry animations. Anything fancier depends on Claude hand-writing HyperFrames captions.html each run.

Corrections to the prior evaluation:
1. Motion graphics lowered from 3 to 2. AIEV owns zero templates. Its 20 "video styles" are only prompt text, and no demo shows the visual quality.
2. The "no overlay" claim is overstated. The short-form-video skill puts the face video inside the HyperFrames composition, with motion-graphics layers on top. That skill assumes a 1920x1080 landscape source.
3. The prior evaluation missed an "Auto cut videos" feature: long video into clips, with Gemini-vision subject detection and ffmpeg reframing (reframe.ts, autoCutPlan.ts).
4. The prompt-injection mitigation is weaker than claimed. "Bash" is fully auto-approved and curl is allow-listed, while the .env deny rules cover only the Read, Edit and Write tools.
5. There are 20 skills, not 19.
6. HyperFrames has no NOTICE file upstream.

AIEV is Claude-only (no Codex runner, no MCP), Vietnamese-first, has no stock B-roll and no tests, and has one maintainer. It is best used as a donor of cutting, QC, manifest/Assemble and agent-runner parts, not as the base to fork.
