fit_rationale:
In favour:
- It already implements the user's core idea for Claude: Claude Code (Agent SDK) as the brain, deterministic REST tools and server-enforced gates.
- Its silence and retake cutting is well engineered, and the Remotion manifest/Assemble plus QC gate is solid.

Against:
- It is Claude-only, with no Codex runner or MCP. Adding Codex means a second runner and porting the skills.
- Captions are one basic karaoke style, which is exactly the gap the user wants to close.
- There is no stock B-roll.
- Motion graphics are freeform LLM HTML+GSAP with no templates of its own. The reusable motion-graphics value (389 registry items) is upstream in HyperFrames, which can be used without AIEV.
- The code is Vietnamese-first (filler lexicons, prompts, comments), untested, single-maintainer and about 3 MB, mostly off-goal.

Lowered from 4 to 3. Harvest autoTrim.ts, deadWeight.ts (swapping in ES/EN lexicons), qc.ts, the manifest/Assemble/MusicTrack components and the agent.ts runner pattern into a fresh harness instead of forking.
captions_detail:
Short answer to "and if autobroll has captions but they aren't premium like captions.ai?": AIEV does not solve that. Its captions are the same tier as autobroll's.

Path 1: deterministic Remotion captions (engines/remotion/src/components/CaptionTrack.tsx, read in full).
- Cues of 4-7 words, with absolute-frame word start and end times.
- The active word turns #19c8ff with a scale pop of 1 + 0.1*min(1, 6/len) over 3 frames, plus a drop-shadow glow.
- Words flagged `hi` stay #ffcf4d at weight 800.
- The line sits in a glass pill (rgba(10,16,32,0.52), blur 20px) at 62px Inter, bottom offset 320 on vertical video, with a 4-frame fade and 18 px rise per cue.
- Everything is a constant. The schema (captionWordSchema) is only {text, start, end, hi}.
- It has no presets, no emoji, no bounce, slide or typewriter entries, no outline or stroke styles, no dynamic placement or face avoidance, and no animated emphasis beyond colour.

Related components:
- SubtitleTrack.tsx is a plain translated subtitle with a few font stacks and backdrop options.
- HighlightTrack.tsx is a separate keyword card (kicker, accent bar, sub pill), not a caption style.

Path 2: LLM-written HyperFrames captions.
- Claude writes captions.html with GSAP per word, following .claude/skills/hyperframes/references/captions.md (a tone-to-style table: hype = scale-pop back.out; social = bounce elastic with coloured pills) and short-form-video/SKILL.md (a captions layer with a layered text-shadow stroke).
- This can look richer, but it is rewritten every run, is not a reusable preset library, and its quality is unverified.

Upstream HyperFrames also ships captions-overlay and embedded-captions skills, which are worth checking directly. To reach Captions.ai or Submagic level, the user still has to build a preset library of caption components: entry and emphasis animations, emoji and keyword metadata chosen by the LLM, and stroke, shadow and placement presets.
motion_graphics_detail:
Engine: HyperFrames (hyperframes ^0.7.81, Apache-2.0 per the lockfile and gh api). HTML/CSS plus GSAP 3.14.2 from jsDelivr, rendered frame by frame in headless Chrome by jobs/sceneRender.ts into one MP4 per scene. Remotion then plays that MP4 full-frame (SceneClip.tsx, scene.render).

Authoring is 100% LLM-written for each video. AIEV ships no scene templates. The 20 "video styles" (assets/video-styles/video-styles.json, seeded from videoStyles.ts) are only prose art and motion directions.

The guidance comes from markdown skills:
- short-form-video: 4 always-on layers, with the face video as a wrapper inside the composition and BOTTOM/FULLSCREEN modes animated by expo.inOut. Scene overlays sit on top of the face, so overlay compositing does happen inside HyperFrames. The prescription assumes a 1920x1080 landscape source.
- noti-tiktok-vn: keyword pop and zoom types synced to SFX.
- hyperframes/*: transition catalogue, 9 palettes, typography, motion principles.
- make-a-video/references/catalog-intent-map.md: maps requests to registry blocks such as data-chart, yt-lower-third, whip-pan, cinematic-zoom and glitch. It notes the registry has no kinetic-type block, so kinetic type is hand-built.

Upstream heygen-com/hyperframes has 165 blocks and 224 components (389 in total), reachable through `npx hyperframes add`.

Deterministic Remotion extras:
- ZoomWrapper keyframe punch-ins (linear, out and inOut eases, face-biased origin of 50% 38%).
- HighlightTrack cards with a pop and an accent-bar sweep.
- SfxTrack using atFrame and mediaStart.

The 86 SFX files have unknown licensing and are not for commercial use. No music-beat detection exists in the server or Remotion path; zooms are placed on word or SFX timestamps by the LLM.

Net: a working render path for LLM-authored motion graphics, with non-deterministic quality and no owned templates.
llm_integration_detail:
Claude only, through @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk.

apps/server/src/agent.ts:
- Calls query() with cwd = repo root, permissionMode 'acceptEdits' and allowedTools [Read, Write, Edit, Glob, Grep, Bash, TodoWrite, Skill].
- maxTurns comes from settings for 'final' sessions, otherwise 100. settingSources is ['project','user'] and systemPrompt is the claude_code preset.
- Prepends CLAUDE.md, resumes by sdkSessionId and applies the per-session model and effort.
- Auto-resumes after a 10 s delay, capped by aiMaxAttempts with progress detection. A code comment notes that resumed sessions once used 34% of spend.
- A final gate re-prompts until outputs/<id>-vN.mp4 exists and meta.status is 'done'.
- Auth: Claude Code subscription login, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, or CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN.

apps/server/src/aiText.ts makes one-shot tool-less calls (maxTurns 1, allowedTools []) for clip picking and publishing metadata.

apps/server/src/editPrompt.ts is a 545-line Vietnamese prompt. It has a prompt-injection guard and states every switch as ON or OFF. The agent drives the tools by curl-ing localhost:6869 REST endpoints (auto-trim analyze and apply, qc, illustrations, brand logos, thumbnail, publish, jobs). The server backs this up with 409 refusals.

Weaknesses:
- There is no MCP server.
- There is no Codex or OpenAI runner. routes/providers.ts only detects ~/.codex/auth.json and says OpenAI is unused.
- Security is weaker than advertised. Bash is fully auto-approved and Bash(curl:*) is allow-listed. The .env deny rules in .claude/settings.json apply only to the Read, Edit and Write tools, so a transcript-borne injection could still use Bash and curl. The 'user' setting source pulls in the host's personal skills.

The skills are plain SKILL.md markdown, so porting them to Codex AGENTS.md or skills is feasible. The runner, resume and cost logic are specific to the Agent SDK.
license_risks:
- **AIEV code:** MIT, verified in LICENSE and the root package.json.
- **Remotion** (remotion and @remotion/*: "SEE LICENSE IN LICENSE.md"): free for individuals and companies of up to 3 people. Larger teams need a paid Company License, which the README acknowledges.
- **@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk 0.3.220:** "SEE LICENSE IN README.md", under Anthropic commercial terms. Usage is billed to the user.
- **GSAP 3.14.2:** loaded from the jsDelivr CDN inside the scenes. Its no-charge Standard License (Webflow) is not OSI-approved.
- **HyperFrames:** Apache-2.0. Upstream has only a LICENSE file (no NOTICE). AIEV's .claude/skills/hyperframes* look adapted from upstream but carry no Apache attribution or license header, so redistribution needs attribution added.
- **SFX:** the 86 bundled files are collected from assorted sources with licensing unknown. assets/sound-effects/README.md says not for commercial video, so do not reuse them.
- **Logos and branding:** the 123 brand logos are their owners' trademarks and are excluded from MIT. The noti.vn name and logo must be replaced.
- **sharp 0.35.x:** Apache-2.0, with LGPL-3.0 libvips binaries as a transitive dependency (dynamic linking, fine).
- **Paid APIs:** Gemini and Soniox.
- **Font:** Inter woff2 subsets are bundled (OFL).

summary:
LeonSooLab/openchatcut is a dead fork: a v0.1.2 snapshot of 0xsline/OpenChatCut, 915 commits behind upstream. Upstream is an AGPL, Chinese-first, local-first "open-source ChatCut alternative": a multitrack Remotion editor with an in-app agent and an MCP bridge. I re-read the code and most claims hold, but the most important one for this user is wrong.

(a) Cutting. "Delete word = delete video" works only for AUDIO items. In src/editor/TimelineComposition.tsx, keptSegments() is called only inside AudioClip. Video items render through MediaFill as one continuous OffthreadVideo from srcInFrame. The code says so directly:
- reduce.ts editedDuration: "video+transcript 走连续渲染" (video with a transcript uses continuous rendering).
- The delete_text tool description: "a VIDEO clip always plays continuously from srcInFrame — deleting its words cuts NOTHING … To cut a video clip use split_item / edit_item".
Upstream's src/agent/tools/schemas/transcript-tools.ts still carries the same warning. So for a talking-head video, clean_script, delete_text and apply_script do not remove fillers, silences or retakes from the picture. The LLM would have to work out split and trim ranges itself, which contradicts the talking-head skill ("Never … place spoken content with edit_item / split_item").
On top of that, the agent's transcribe_track hardcodes languageCode 'zh' (transcript-tools.ts lines 245 and 338), and transcribe-jobs.ts has DEFAULT_LANG = 'zh'. Spanish or English creators get Chinese-forced ASR unless the code is patched. The filler set is English plus Chinese only.

(b) Captions. There are 22 static CSS presets, and the active word only swaps color or background. Several presets (plain, netflix, bold-outline and others) set the same highlight color as the text color, so they show no highlight at all. The fork has no per-word animation, emoji or automatic emphasis. Upstream adds 4 easing presets (fade-up, pop, word-pop, karaoke-pulse) and still has no emoji or emphasis.

(c) Motion graphics are real and its best area: 235 Remotion JSX templates (211 + 15 + 9), of which only 20 are vertical. The LLM can write new graphics through create_motion_graphic_from_code, compiled by a Babel "sandbox" whose own comment says it is not a hard VM boundary. There is also frame verification that returns images, 10 zoom shapes, 16 transition shaders and 39 sound effects. The vertical templates are simple (about 1.6 KB of spring text cards), and the template comment "Scraped templates" raises provenance questions.

(d) Color is a conservative auto-grade (a CSS filter clamped to 0.94–1.08), a .cube LUT shader and 14 (not 17) short hand-written "film look" shaders.

(e) LLM wiring. An MCP server exposes 91 editor tools to Claude Code or Codex, but only while a browser editor tab is open and polling. The bearer token is optional, so the endpoint is open when OPENCHATCUT_MCP_TOKEN is unset. The built-in agent is API-key only (9 providers). Some tools, such as find_highlights, call that API-key model even when Claude Code is driving. Upstream adds `claude -p` stream-json and Codex app-server runtimes, which I verified.

(f) Rendering uses Remotion renderMedia with a hardware-encoder fallback, plus ProRes 4444 export.

On the user's question ("what if autobroll has captions but they are not premium like captions.ai"): OpenChatCut does not close that gap. Its captions are at the same karaoke-highlight level, and even upstream only adds 4 simple motions. Its core cutting model also does not cut talking-head video. What is worth taking from it is the motion-graphics design (LLM-written Remotion JSX plus sandbox plus frame verification), the MCP harness pattern and upstream's Claude Code/Codex runners. Take the design ideas, not the code, unless the user accepts AGPL.
captions_detail:
Files read in the fork:
- src/captions/styles.ts: 22 CAPTION_STYLES, each a static object (font, size ratio, weight, color, highlightColor, optional highlightBackground, stroke, textShadow, textTransform, displayMode 'stacked', wordsPerPage, wholeLine). A comment says the first 9 "follow PRD §4.17 (bundle only evidences 'Bubble Pop' — preset values are server-side)", which points to reverse-engineering of commercial ChatCut. Several presets have highlightColor equal to color and no highlightBackground (plain, netflix, bold-outline, dogme, deyi-card), so they show no karaoke highlight at all.
- src/captions/renderStyles.ts: wordStyle(preset, active) only swaps color/background. containerStyle() places the block on a 3x3 anchor grid with offset ratios.
- src/captions/CaptionsLayer.tsx: renders plain <span>s inside the Remotion composition, so preview and export match. No spring, interpolate or scale. Supports multi-lane captions and a bilingual translated line.
- src/captions/types.ts and resolve.ts: pagination, per-word overrides, and re-timing onto the edited timeline.
- src/captions/segmenter.ts: CJK-focused line breaking.
Grepping src/captions and src/agent/tools/caption* for emoji, emphas, keyword, spring(, interpolate( and scale( found nothing.
Upstream src/captions/captionMotion.ts (read) adds 4 presets: fade-up (translateY with easeOutCubic), pop (page scale with easeOutBack), word-pop (each word scales from 0.72 at its start time) and karaoke-pulse (sine scale of 1.08 while spoken). Still no emoji, automatic emphasis, per-word SFX or keyword color logic.
Verdict: basic karaoke captions, well below Captions.ai/Submagic. The retiming logic in resolve.ts is the only piece worth reusing, and it is AGPL.
motion_graphics_detail:
Verified in the fork:
- src/template-host.ts: Babel-compiles `({item}) => JSX` with a regex blocklist (import, eval, .constructor, window., fetch(, timers and more), shadows 36 globals and whitelists the Remotion API. Its header says: "This is hardening, NOT a hard VM boundary … PRODUCTION must additionally run templates in a sandboxed iframe or QuickJS".
- src/agent/tools/mg-code-tools.ts: create_motion_graphic_from_code compiles through the sandbox and registers an asset with editable properties.
- src/agent/tools/frames-tool.ts: view_timeline_frames and view_asset_frames return base64 images or a contact sheet, and mcp.ts forwards them as MCP image content.

Templates (parsed from the JSON):
- openchatcut-templates.json: 211 templates. 210 are 1920x1080 and 1 is 1080x1920. Categories: 102 uncategorized "Style Showcase" families, 35 data-visualization, 27 title-cards, 12 infographics, 10 lower-thirds, 8 talking-head overlays, 8 text-effects, 5 quote cards. 138 use spring(), 117 use SVG, code averages 6.3 KB, and only 187 of 211 have a propSchema.
- social-shorts-templates.json: 15 vertical templates, averaging about 1.6 KB each. They are simple spring-scaled text cards (keyword pop, caption bar, name bar, CTA, checklist and similar) with Chinese default text.
- koubo-scenes-templates.json: 9 templates (5 at 16:9, 4 vertical).
- 236 thumbnails.

Other motion pieces:
- src/editor/zoom.ts: zoom easing shapes including punch, snap, whip-in, pulse, bounce and slow-push.
- src/gl/shaders: 16 transitions (whip-pan, glitch-cut, impact-shake, rack-focus and others).
- src/gl/fx: about 46 effect shaders.
- assets/sound-effects: 39 MP3s.
- src/editor/design-presets.ts: 24 id entries by my count (the earlier claim was 26).
- src/agent/tools/mg-video-tools.ts: renders ProRes locally, then transcodes to VP9-alpha WebM in the E2B cloud sandbox, falling back to opaque H.264. export_motion_graphic_prores gives ProRes 4444 .mov.

The architecture is the right shape and rich for open source. The shipped content, however, is template-grade and mostly 16:9, and the 20 vertical templates are simple. Output quality for reels depends on the LLM writing good JSX.
llm_integration_detail:
Fork, verified:
1. src/agent/client.ts creates createAnthropic / createOpenAI / createOpenAICompatible clients pointing at `${ORIGIN}/llm`, a server proxy that injects API keys. shared/llm-providers.ts lists 9 providers: anthropic, openai, gemini, kimi, qwen, glm, deepseek, minimax, mistral. There is no Claude Code or Codex CLI as the built-in brain.
2. server/external-agent/mcp.ts is a Streamable HTTP MCP server with 5 control tools plus the tools each editor registers. I counted 91 tool schemas in src/agent/tools*. Image results are returned as MCP image content.
3. server/external-agent/broker.ts and src/agent/useExternalAgentBridge.ts: the browser tab registers itself and long-polls /api/external-agent/poll. Tool calls are queued to that tab (35 s online window, 180 s default timeout), so there is no headless operation.
4. server/plugins/external-agent.ts lines 48–49: auth is `!token || header === Bearer token`, so the endpoint is unauthenticated unless OPENCHATCUT_MCP_TOKEN is set. It is mounted as Vite dev-server middleware.
5. The root .mcp.json points Claude Code at http://localhost:5199/api/external-mcp/mcp.
6. Some tools call the built-in API-key model internally. For example, find_highlights in highlight-tool.ts imports generateAgentText from ../client, so driving through Claude Code or Codex does not fully remove the need for API keys.

Upstream, verified:
- server/claude-code/turn-runner.ts spawns `claude -p … --output-format stream-json --mcp-config <private> --strict-mcp-config --allowedTools mcp__<server>__* --disallowedTools Bash,Read,Edit,Write,Glob,Grep,WebFetch,WebSearch,Task,Agent…`.
- server/codex/app-server.ts spawns `codex app-server --listen stdio://` and talks JSON-RPC to it.
- Upstream also adds cli/ (the occ CLI), server/agent-runs and 36 external-agent files. The broker and poll files remain, so upstream likely still depends on an editor tab; I did not verify this fully.

fit_rationale:
Do not fork LeonSooLab/openchatcut. It is a v0.1.2 snapshot 915 commits behind upstream.

Upstream 0xsline/OpenChatCut is also a poor base for this user, for four reasons:
1. Problem #1 (cutting talking-head video) is not solved by its text-editing model. Word deletion, filler cleanup and silence cleanup only re-time audio items, and video clips play continuously, as the code and its own tool description say.
2. ASR is Chinese-first, and the fork's agent hardcodes 'zh'.
3. Problem #3 (premium captions) is not solved: static presets plus 4 simple motions, and no emoji or emphasis.
4. AGPL network copyleft combined with Remotion's company license (required for for-profit companies with 4 or more employees) constrains a commercial product.

Its real value is as a design reference:
- the motion-graphics pipeline (LLM-written Remotion JSX, sandbox compile, editable properties, frame-image verification);
- the pattern of exposing deterministic editor tools over MCP;
- upstream's Claude Code (`claude -p` stream-json with a private MCP config and denied built-in tools) and Codex app-server runners, which is exactly the user's harness idea.

Scores: 3 for the fork. Upstream would be about 5 if AGPL and Remotion licensing are acceptable and the team is willing to add video-segment cutting and Spanish ASR. As a code donor for a closed or permissive product it is about 2: reimplement the ideas and do not copy files.

license_risks:
1. AGPL-3.0-or-later (the LICENSE file is AGPL v3, and package.json says "AGPL-3.0-or-later"). Copying any file into autobroll makes autobroll AGPL, including a hosted service, which must offer its source to users.
2. src/agent/skills/ is adapted from ChatCut-Inc/agent-plugin under GPL-3.0-only, per NOTICE.md.
3. Remotion (4.0.489 in the fork) uses the Remotion License, which is source-available, not OSI. Its LICENSE.md in remotion-dev/remotion grants the Free License to "a for-profit organization with up to 3 employees", so a Company License is required at 4 or more. Pairing a non-OSI dependency with AGPL is awkward when distributing the Electron build.
4. Provenance: template-host.ts says "Scraped templates often carry a DANGLING bgImage", and styles.ts says "The first 9 presets follow PRD §4.17 (bundle only evidences 'Bubble Pop' — preset values are server-side)". Together these suggest templates and caption presets reverse-engineered from commercial ChatCut, so copyright is unclear for the 211 templates and 236 thumbnails.
5. Fonts: assets/fonts/LICENSES.md lists only 4 OFL fonts. HarmonyOS Sans, 3 Huxiaobo fonts and 2 Pangmen fonts are free for commercial use but not open source.
6. The 39 sound-effect MP3s and the Canon and Sony LUT .cube files have no license or attribution file in the tree.
7. ffmpeg-static ships GPL ffmpeg binaries.
8. Cloud dependencies: AssemblyAI (ASR), E2B (alpha WebM and run_code), Firecrawl, S3 SDK.
GSAP is not used, and there are no model-weight license issues beyond @huggingface/transformers models fetched at runtime.

summary:
Mostly confirmed against the code, with some corrections. This is a real VEED open-source, agent-driven caption and graphics tool. Its architecture is close to the user's harness idea: a skill plus AGENTS.md make Claude Code, Codex or Gemini the brain, and deterministic CLI commands do the work. I found no LLM SDK or API calls in cli/src, pipeline, prep or veed. The default caption path makes zero model calls.

**Captions (strongest area).** refs/tags.json v3 indexes exactly 42 recipe modules. Each has recipe.ts, recipe.md and template.wv; I counted the files. There are also 6 classic presets. I read hook-114-peak/recipe.ts and it matches the claims: a 45 ms per-glyph stagger from real word delays, a bigPop scale .4 to 1.28 to 1, a spinning clip-path star and an underline that draws in. I read classic-lib.ts and it has 7 animation modes plus outline, shadow, bars and a frosted plate. Only 31 of the 42 recipes are tagged 9:16; 11 are 16:9 only. There is no emoji anywhere (the only pictograph found was a ✓ in docs). Emphasis is heuristic: the digit-bearing word, else the longest. There are no word-synced SFX and no punch zooms.

**Cutting.** These are real, pro-grade primitives (speech-probe, apply-edl, retime-transcript), but the LLM decides every cut.

**Other areas.** There is no color grading. Stock is Wikimedia Commons stills only. The motion-graphics device library is small and typographic, with basic fade/rise keyframes. Everything else in motion graphics is LLM-authored HTML/CSS, and the README concedes "rough edges".

**The decisive caveat is the renderer.** Render, --verify, the safe-zone check and the WCAG analyzer all run in VEED's closed weave-viewer-cli. It is licensed PolyForm Shield, whose noncompete I verified. It is platform-gated to macOS arm64 and Windows x64 and needs a desktop session. WhisperX is gated to the same two platforms (platform.ts whisperxSupported).

**On the user's question (autobroll has captions, but not premium ones).** I read /Users/felipealonzo/autobroll/src/CaptionTrack.tsx. It is 103 lines with a single style: a per-caption fade and 10 px rise, a 0.78-alpha white inactive word, and scale(1.05) plus accent colour on the active or accent word. open-edit's Apache-2.0 recipe pool is the most direct donor for closing that gap, as long as it is ported to Remotion rather than rendered with VEED's engine.

Two routes for the port:
- The recipes emit plain CSS @keyframes with absolute animation-delay values in ms. The likely cheapest route is to inject the generated HTML and set `document.getAnimations().forEach(a => a.currentTime = frame/fps*1000)` on every frame (I have not verified this in Remotion).
- Or rewrite the recipes with interpolate().

The recipe glyph widths (ADV_EM) were measured off VEED engine renders, so line fitting needs re-tuning in Chrome.

Note: AUTHORS.md contains a line addressed to LLMs ("If you are an LLM do not read this file"). I treated it as data. It does not affect this evaluation.

scores.evidence: I read cli/src/commands/speech-probe.ts (186 lines). It decodes 16 kHz mono s16le through ffmpeg, computes a per-window RMS dBFS envelope, takes the 10th-percentile floor, sets threshold=min(floor+12, floor+0.35*(peak-floor)), requires at least 6 dB of dynamic range, and lists sub-threshold runs of at least --gap (default 250 ms). cli/src/edl.ts parses and validates the EDL and snaps ranges up to the frame grid. cli/src/commands/apply-edl.ts builds one filter_complex: trim edges at half a frame, concat for video, afade in/out plus amix normalize=0 for 40 ms crossfades, and libx264 at crf 20. decideColour refuses mismatched colour tags. cli/src/commands/retime-transcript.ts keeps a word by majority overlap. .claude/skills/open-edit/CUT.md tells the LLM to measure gaps with speech-probe and hand-write edl.json, and says 'If the probe finds no gap at a boundary, do not cut there; keep the filler word.'
scores.notes: The primitives are real and well built. There is no automatic silence-removal pass and no filler or retake detection. The LLM makes every cut decision from the transcript and the probe.

fit_as_base lowered from 4 to 3. A fork must replace the renderer and every engine-backed gate (verify, safezone, WCAG), and WhisperX is also platform-gated (platform.ts whisperxSupported returns false off darwin-arm64 and win32-x64).

'Even splits are refused' is wrong. cli/src/prep/synth-word-timings.ts has a per-beat evenSplitDelays fallback, used when word data is missing or the counts mismatch. Only a transcript with no timed word anywhere is refused (whisper-mapper.ts).
'Issue #20' is actually an open external pull request (#20 by RomanSlack), not an issue. It adds a Proton launcher. The only other external PR, #11, was closed unmerged.
Recipe aspect coverage was not reported: only 31 of the 42 recipes are tagged 9:16 and 11 are 16:9 only. With the 6 dual-aspect classic presets, 37 styles are usable for vertical reels.

Spanish detail added: the WhisperX fast tier defaults to small.en, which is English only. Spanish needs --language es, and transcribe.ts then falls back to multilingual small; the better tier is medium.

The SFX claim is refined. fal.ts supports sfx, music and speech kinds (bring your own key, --model required, no default), but there is no SFX library and no word-synced SFX. mix-audio.ts does voice-ducked mixing with sidechaincompress.

The VEED login is optional, not a hard requirement. init does not require it and the WhisperX path runs offline. NOTICE's statement that transcription is performed against the VEED service is out of date compared with the code.

Size corrected: the recipe and pipeline TS is about 12.8k lines (60 files, 48 recipe modules), not 9.4k. cli/src is about 17.9k lines. There are also 5 integration tests in cli/tests-integration, and no published tests cover the recipes, devices or lint-template.

Renderer platform nuance: the weave-renderer-public-releases README still says macOS arm64 only, but Windows x64 assets have shipped since weave-v0.9.0. The latest release, weave-v0.11.0 (2026-09-22), is confirmed.

Removed the unverified claim that fonts fall back silently when offline. Verified only that recipes load Google Fonts through <link>, and that the Claude sandbox allowlist includes fonts.googleapis.com.
Supply-chain claim clarified: session-start runs a bare init that self-applies patch/minor CLI updates. Renderer updates require explicit approval.

Confirmed without change: Apache-2.0 for the repo; the PolyForm Shield noncompete text; 42 plus 6 recipes; the hook-114-peak mechanics; the classic-lib modes; the speech-probe math; the apply-edl graph; no LLM SDK in the code; the three SessionStart hooks; 135 KB of prompt prose; the no-op CI; the missing tests/ dir; no emoji; no color grading; Wikimedia-only stills; a read-only preview; and that all 33 reusable-part paths exist.
captions_detail:
**Pipeline.** The flow runs:
1. transcript.json, from any of three providers: VEED; WhisperX (default model small.en, English only; --language es falls back to small); or `whisper` mapping WhisperX, whisper.cpp or OpenAI verbose_json JSON.
2. whisper-mapper.ts normalises the transcript, interpolates untimed words, and refuses only a transcript with no timed words at all.
3. cli/src/prep/synth-word-timings.ts turns it into word-timings.json. Beats are the transcript segments, each word gets an absolute animation-delay, and a beat with missing or mismatched word data falls back to an even split.
4. sample-style.ts makes a seeded, aspect-filtered draw across the 42 v3 recipes, weighted by facet energy matched to transcript energy.
5. generate-recipe runs the compiled recipe.ts, which emits template.wv as HTML plus CSS keyframes.

**Recipe vocabulary (verified in hook-114-peak).**
- Glyph-by-glyph gIn at a 45 ms stagger, compressed so it finishes before the end of the cue.
- A punch line split from up to 3 balanced setup lines.
- An accent word with bigPop (scale .4 to 1.28 to 1).
- A pink clip-path star that pops in and then spins.
- An underline drawn with scaleX.
- Size ladders that demote when verify reports bounds failures.
- Glyph advance widths (ADV_EM) measured off real engine renders.

Facets across the pool include char-blur-in, char-glow-random, illuminate-flicker, stop-motion, word-pop-active, torn-paper, doodle-overlay, arc-headline, laurel-badge, speech-bubble, glow-text and word-plate.

**Classic presets** (refs/html/classic/classic-lib.ts; simple, karl, lowkey, rizz, mint, glass):
- modes karaoke, colourHighlight, highlight, dropIn, floatInBottom, flipClock and fadeInPre;
- an 8-way outline through text-shadow, a drop shadow, per-line or per-word bars, and a frosted plate.

**Emphasis** is heuristic: the digit-bearing word, else the longest. It becomes semantic only when the LLM customises a --module copy.

**Placement and checks.**
- measure-placement.ts uses ffmpeg only to estimate motion, detail and skin.
- safe-zone.ts holds the margins.
- safezone-check and wcag-pass run through the engine binary.

**Missing:** emoji (none found by a codepoint scan), SFX tied to words, and automatic zoom on emphasis.

**Porting to autobroll/Remotion.** The output is standard CSS keyframes with absolute ms delays, so it can be driven per frame through WAAPI (set currentTime on every animation) or rewritten with interpolate(). Glyph-width constants need re-measuring in Chrome, and fonts come from Google Fonts. By comparison, autobroll's src/CaptionTrack.tsx (103 lines) has one style: a fade plus 10 px rise per caption, and scale(1.05) plus accent colour on the active word.
motion_graphics_detail:
**Engine.** The closed weave-viewer-cli renders .wv files: HTML plus a CSS subset, with a single timeline driven by @keyframes and animation-delay, and no JS. pipeline/director-brief.md (32.5 KB) sets the authoring contract and ENGINE LIMITS, all decided by probe renders: no grid, radial-gradient or mask; blur and box-shadow do not animate; skewX is ignored; text-stroke never paints.

**Authoring.** Creative (face-1), REMIX and NO VIDEO runs are written inline by the orchestrating LLM, following DESIGN.md and a per-run design system (pipeline/design/system.ts, with checkLadder, checkFonts and check).

**Building blocks.**
- pipeline/recipes/devices.ts: 11 builders (lowerThird, statBlock, dataRail, titleCard, heroFigure, badgeLockup, kicker, divider, tickScale, accentWord, groundShadow). Their motion is mostly an opacity plus translateY rise; heroFigure uses baked spring keyframes.
- geometry.ts: alongArc, lattice, springKeyframes, starPolygon, arcRectPolygon.
- svg-clip.ts: converts an SVG logo into a clip-path polygon.
- type.ts: optical tracking and type ladders.

**Gates.** lint-template.ts (static) runs first, then the engine's --verify (bounds, never-visible, occluded).

**Missing.** No prebuilt b-roll insert templates: no icons, charts, UI mockups, count-ups or Lottie. No punch zooms on the footage and no SFX library.

**Caveats.** The README's showcase was driven by a frontier model and says motion graphics have rough edges. Nothing in the repo consumes the devices, and they have no tests.
llm_integration_detail:
**Install and hooks.** Install with `npx skills add veedstudio/open-edit --skill open-edit`, then run `claude`, `codex` or `gemini`. SessionStart hooks in .claude/settings.json, .codex/hooks.json (matcher startup|resume|clear|compact) and .gemini/settings.json run `npx --yes @veedstudio/openedit-cli session-start <agent>`. That command runs a bare init in-process, which self-updates the CLI by patch or minor versions, and returns a context note telling the agent to read AGENTS.md. Gemini gets the note as JSON. CLAUDE.md is just `@AGENTS.md`. The Claude settings also set a network sandbox allowlist (veed.io, Google Fonts, GitHub).

**Code and tools.** No model SDK and no API key appear in the code. The agent shells out to CLI commands and reads their stdout; there is no MCP server and no tool schemas.

**Routes in SKILL.md.**
- FAST PATH: transcribe, prep, sample-style, generate-recipe and mux-audio, with zero tokens.
- Variant B, creative face-1: the agent authors the .wv inline.
- REMIX: a blend of donor sheets.
- NO VIDEO.
- ANALYSE: an opt-in step.

**Prompt size and seams.** Prompt prose totals 135 KB across SKILL, CUT, DESIGN, STYLE, GENERATION, TRANSCRIPTION, director-brief and AGENTS. The transcript is a single seam (runs/<key>/transcript.json) that any provider can feed.

red_flags: The renderer weave-viewer-cli is closed and licensed PolyForm Shield 1.0.0. Its noncompete bars 'providing any product that competes with the software or any product the licensor... provides', which almost certainly covers an AI reel editor.
Render, --verify, the safe-zone check and the WCAG analyzer all depend on that binary. Without it the repo only generates HTML/CSS documents.

Platform gating: rendering and WhisperX both require macOS arm64 or Windows x64 (platform.ts), plus a real desktop session. There is no Linux, headless or cloud path; Proton exists only as open external PR #20.
The repo is a one-way Copybara mirror of a private monorepo. Public CI is a no-op echo, the root `test` script points at a missing tests/ dir, and external PRs do not land (#11 was closed unmerged).
Supply chain: every SessionStart runs `npx --yes` for the latest CLI, and bare init self-applies patch/minor updates.
Missing features: color grading, stock video b-roll (Wikimedia stills only), filler and retake detection, emoji, word-synced SFX, punch zooms, and a motion-graphics template catalogue.
Emphasis in the deterministic path is heuristic (digit-bearing or longest word), not semantic.
The default fast transcription tier is small.en, which is English only. Spanish needs an explicit --language es.
11 of the 42 recipes are 16:9 only.
About 135 KB of rigid prompt prose makes creative runs token-heavy and brittle to adapt.
The engine's CSS subset (no JS, grid, mask or radial-gradient; blur and box-shadow do not animate; no text-stroke) limits motion richness.
The project is very young (created 2026-07-22), and its engine floor moves with each release (minEngine 0.11.0).
license_risks:
**The repo itself.** The editor, CLI, recipes, skill and docs are Apache-2.0. They are safe to fork or copy as long as LICENSE and NOTICE are kept.

**The renderer.** The binary that install-engine downloads from veedstudio/weave-renderer-public-releases is PolyForm Shield 1.0.0. I verified the text in LICENSE-binary.md. Its noncompete covers competing products even when they are free or on other platforms. Shipping the binary, or depending on it, in the user's AI reel editor is a serious risk. The README only grants commercial use of the videos produced with it.

**Recipe provenance.** The recipes appear to be transplanted from reference hooks (directory names like 'hook-126 Comp 1-peak' and 'transplanted pink — kept verbatim'). That is a low-risk provenance note: visual styles are generally not copyrightable, and the code is Apache-2.0.

**Remotion.** open-edit has no Remotion dependency. The user's autobroll does (remotion and @remotion/cli 4.0.380), so porting the recipes there inherits Remotion's license, which requires a paid company license above the free tier (individuals and companies of up to 3 people are free).

**Everything else.**
- No GSAP.
- The runtime dependency culori is MIT.
- WhisperX is BSD-2, and its alignment and ASR models carry their own licenses.
- VEED transcription and Fabric fall under VEED's terms and credits; fal falls under the user's own terms.
- Google Fonts are OFL. The Inter and STIX Two woff2 subsets on the login page are OFL.

summary:
Short answer to the user's question: switching to OpenMontage would not fix the "captions exist but aren't Captions.ai-level" problem. Its captions are the same basic karaoke tier. There is a single Remotion component, remotion-composer/src/components/CaptionOverlay.tsx:
- Words are grouped into pages (4 per page in the TalkingHead path; the component default is 6) inside a rounded translucent box.
- Each page enters with a spring fade and slide-up.
- The active word changes to highlightColor with a glow; upcoming words are dimmed.
- The box is fixed at the bottom (paddingBottom 80).
- There are no presets, emphasis, emoji, per-word scale or pop, or face-aware placement.

The burn tool (tools/video/remotion_caption_burn.py) exposes even fewer controls than the component: only words_per_page, font_size, highlight_color, corrections and overlays. @remotion/captions is a dependency, but nothing in src imports it.

The strongest premium-caption lead is upstream heygen-com/hyperframes (Apache-2.0, 52.7k stars). Its skills/embedded-captions contains dna/, modes/, themes/, scripts/ and CATALOG.md. OpenMontage's PROVENANCE.md says it deliberately did not vendor that skill or talking-head-recut. I have not verified upstream's quality; it needs its own evaluation.

What OpenMontage actually is: an agent-agnostic "skills + tools + pipelines" harness with no LLM API calls in its code.
- CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md say only "read AGENT_GUIDE.md" (48 KB), and CODEX.md points to the same guide.
- The agent follows pipeline_defs/*.yaml and the per-stage director skills, and calls Python tools through `python -c` with registry.discover() and Tool().execute().
- lib/checkpoint.py deterministically enforces stage order, required human approvals and JSON-schema validation of artifacts.

Verified status of each problem:
- Cutting: FFmpeg silencedetect only. Filler-word and false-start removal exist only as LLM prose in skills (skills/creative/video-editing.md, and the talking-head scene and edit directors).
- Grading: 7 static FFmpeg presets plus a .cube LUT. The intensity blend looks inverted.
- B-roll: good multi-source stock retrieval with CLIP ranking, used only by documentary-montage. The talking-head composition has no cutaway layer, and the generic FFmpeg overlay operation has timing bugs.
- Motion graphics: 11 generic Remotion card and chart overlays with an 8-frame fade. The HyperFrames generator only writes a fade-up skeleton, and the richer motion know-how is vendored HeyGen prose.

A 19-clip Pixabay SFX pack is vendored from HyperFrames but is not wired in. On review I lowered broll_stock, motion_graphics_broll, render_pipeline and maintainability from 3 to 2.

scores.evidence:
Read tools/video/silence_cutter.py (481 lines, v0.1.0, EXPERIMENTAL). It runs `ffmpeg silencedetect=noise=-35dB:d=0.5`, regex-parses the start and end times, and inverts them into speech segments with 0.08 s padding. There are three modes:
- remove: re-encodes each segment with libx264, CRF 18, then concat -c copy.
- speed_up: applies setpts and an atempo chain to the silences.
- mark: writes JSON.
The talking-head edit-director.md Step 1 calls it. skills/creative/video-editing.md tells the LLM to cut 'um, uh, like' at word boundaries and to keep only the final take after a false start, but no Python implements that. Code search for filler and retake finds only .md files.
scores.notes:
Energy-threshold cutting only, with no transcript-aware or retake logic. Other problems:
- The transcriber (faster-whisper 'base', vad_filter=True, no disfluency prompt) usually drops 'um' and 'uh' from its output, so the prose filler instruction has little to work with.
- Bug in speed_up: speech segments extend 0.08 s into each silence, and the silence segments are not trimmed. The comment says 'merge overlaps', but no merge is done, so about 80 ms is duplicated at every boundary.
- remove mode uses output seeking (-ss after -i) for every segment, which is slow on long inputs.
- Caption timestamps are not remapped after a cut; the captions come from the asset_manifest transcript, which is made before the edit stage.
- No tests.

scores.evidence: Read tools/enhancement/color_grade.py (212 lines, v0.1.0, EXPERIMENTAL). It has 7 hard-coded profiles built from colorbalance, curves and eq (cinematic_warm, cinematic_cool, moody_dark, bright_clean, vintage_film, high_contrast, neutral). It also takes a lut3d .cube path, a custom_vf passthrough, and an intensity option implemented as `split[original][tograde];...;[original][graded]blend=all_mode=normal:all_opacity=<intensity>`. Output is libx264 at CRF 20 with audio copied. The compose-director chains face_enhance, eye_enhance, color_grade and audio_enhance.
scores.notes: Likely bug: FFmpeg blend treats the first input ([original]) as the top layer, and normal mode outputs top*opacity + bottom*(1-opacity). So intensity=0.3 gives 70% graded, the reverse of the documented '0 = original, 1 = full grade'. Intensity is also ignored for LUTs. There is no automatic white balance, exposure analysis, shot matching or skin protection. The only tests are metadata contract tests in tests/contracts/test_phase2_contracts.py (profile count, tool fields), with no test of the filter output.

scores.evidence:
Read remotion-composer/src/components/CaptionOverlay.tsx (177 lines). buildPages groups words by wordsPerPage and pageBreakAfter. Each page is a Sequence with a spring opacity and translateY(20 to 0) entrance. The active word gets highlightColor and a textShadow glow, past words the base color, and upcoming words the color at 0x99 alpha. The box sits at justify flex-end with paddingBottom 80. scores.notes:
Basic karaoke highlight only:
- No style presets, emphasis or keyword detection, or emoji.
- No per-word scale, pop or bounce, no stroke or uppercase styles.
- Fixed bottom placement with no face or safe-zone awareness.
- The tool cannot even set caption color, background or font, although the component supports them.
- For SRT input, word timings are faked by splitting each cue evenly.

@remotion/captions is unused in src. The vendored .agents/skills/hyperframes-creative/frame-presets/*/caption-skin.html files depend on captions.mjs, which is not in the repo. The tool docstring says HyperFrames word-level caption parity is 'explicitly deferred'. There are no tests for the burn tool. This is the same tier as the user's current autobroll captions.

scores.evidence:
Retrieval is real and solid:
- tools/video/stock_sources/ has 16 adapters. pexels.py calls api.pexels.com/videos/search and /v1/search with an orientation filter and picks a rendition up to 1920 wide.
- tools/video/corpus_builder.py fans a query out to the sources, downloads, extracts thumbnails, computes a motion_score and CLIP-embeds each clip.
- lib/clip_embedder.py uses openai/clip-vit-base-patch32.
- tools/video/clip_search.py provides rank_for_slot, find_similar_set (MMR) and diversify.
- tests/tools/test_stock_source_adapters.py exists.
Placement for talking-head is weak. pipeline_defs/talking-head.yaml lists no stock tools (image_selector is only optional in the assets stage), and TalkingHead.tsx has no image, video or cutaway overlay type. The generic FFmpeg `overlay` operation in video_compose.py (_overlay, around line 2746) can put a clip over the speaker with between(t,...) while keeping 0:a.
scores.notes:
Lowered from 3. The search stack alone would be a 3 to 4 and is good donor material, but placement over talking-head speech is effectively missing. The generic _overlay operation has bugs:
- The overlay input is not PTS-shifted to its start time, so a 5 s clip enabled at t=10 shows its last frame frozen.
- The `opacity` input is read but never used.
- scale=w:h stretches the clip without cropping.
CLIP ranking and MMR are wired only into documentary-montage.

scores.notes:
Lowered from 3. The in-repo templates are generic dark-SaaS cards, rendered as opaque h264 with fixed pixel positions, so they break on non-1080x1920 input. There are no zoom punches, icon library or reels UI mockups, and no automatic mapping from transcript beats to inserts; the asset-director picks overlays by hand. Correction to the prior claim of no SFX library: 19 Pixabay SFX (whoosh, pop, riser, impact and others, with a manifest.json) are vendored at .agents/skills/hyperframes-media/assets/sfx/, but no tool or pipeline uses them. Entry files:

scores.notes:
This matches the 'Claude Code or Codex as brain' idea exactly, and switching agents only means running a different CLI in the repo. Weaknesses:
- Control flow is prose the agent is asked to obey (48 KB guide plus a 19 KB compose-director and more).
- Tool calls are `python -c` snippets, not MCP or typed calls.
- BaseTool does not validate inputs against input_schema at execute time.
- The agent can set human_approved itself.
- .codex/prompts has only 3 niche prompts (animated-drawing, backlot, ink-art).

fit_rationale:
The architecture matches the user's idea: a CLI coding agent as the brain, a deterministic Python and FFmpeg tool layer, and YAML pipelines with per-stage skills and schema-validated checkpoints. But it is a poor starting point to fork:
1. AGPL-3.0. Forking, or copying any file, makes the user's editor AGPL, including giving source to users of a hosted service.
2. None of the four hard problems is solved above a basic level, and the relevant tools are experimental, untested, and have the bugs described in the scores:
   - Captions: one generic karaoke style, with fewer controls exposed than the component supports.
   - Cutting: dB-threshold silence removal only.
   - Grading: static presets, with an inverted intensity blend.
   - B-roll: good retrieval, but no talking-head cutaway layer and a buggy generic overlay.
   - Motion graphics: generic card templates plus a skeleton generator.
3. The strongest motion, caption and SFX material is vendored from heygen-com/hyperframes (Apache-2.0) and should be taken from upstream. OpenMontage also deliberately left out the two upstream skills this user most needs, embedded-captions and talking-head-recut.
4. A heavy payload irrelevant to talking-head reels.

Best use: study and reimplement the harness pattern (tool contract, registry, pipeline YAML, checkpoint gate, one agent-entry file per CLI). Reimplement or reference the stock-retrieval design. For premium captions, evaluate HyperFrames upstream directly.
corrections: Scores lowered from 3 to 2 for broll_stock, motion_graphics_broll, render_pipeline and maintainability: the evidence shows basic or buggy behaviour in the talking-head path, and the uncertainty rule applies. fit_as_base lowered from 3 to 2.

An SFX library does exist, contrary to the prior claim of none: 19 Pixabay-licensed clips with a manifest.json are vendored at .agents/skills/hyperframes-media/assets/sfx/ from HeyGen HyperFrames. No tool or pipeline wires them in.

A generic FFmpeg `overlay` operation exists in video_compose.py (_overlay), so a B-roll cutaway over the speaker's audio is not impossible. However, the overlay clip is not PTS-shifted, so it freezes or plays out of sync; the opacity input is ignored; and scaling stretches without cropping.

Filler-word handling is not only a 'false starts' mention. skills/creative/video-editing.md explicitly tells the LLM to cut 'um, uh, like' using word timestamps. It is still prose only, and faster-whisper with vad_filter usually omits those fillers, so it is unreliable.

The harness is not purely prose. lib/checkpoint.py _enforce_stage_prerequisites deterministically blocks stage advancement without completed, schema-valid and approved predecessors. However, BaseTool never validates tool inputs against input_schema, and .codex/prompts has only 3 niche prompts.

color_grade: the intensity blend appears inverted, because [original] is the top layer in blend normal mode, so output = original*intensity + graded*(1-intensity). Also, tests are not fully absent: there are metadata-only contract tests in tests/contracts/test_phase2_contracts.py.

silence_cutter speed_up mode duplicates about 80 ms at each speech/silence boundary: the padded speech segments overlap the untrimmed silence segments, and the 'merge overlaps' comment has no matching code.

remotion_caption_burn passes only wordsPerPage, fontSize and highlightColor, so caption color, background and font are not controllable from the tool. The SRT input path fakes word timing by splitting each cue evenly. The component default is 6 words per page; the 4 comes from TalkingHead and the tool.

Size counts: the tree has 2,571 entries, but only 2,115 are files. .agents has 994 files (1,267 entries), .claude has 432 files (519 entries), and skills/ has 157 .md files (174 entries). 167 .py files are under tools/ and 517 .py files exist in total.

Clarified that requirements.txt includes openai>=2.44 and google-genai. They are used for the Sora, Veo and Lyria media-generation APIs, not as an LLM brain, so the claim of no hard-wired LLM still holds.

Confirmed the Remotion License text: free for individuals, for-profit organizations with up to 3 employees, and non-profits; otherwise a Company License from remotion.pro is required. The license also notes that terms change in Remotion 5.0.
Confirmed the GSAP Standard License restriction against use in no-code visual animation builders that compete with Webflow.

Confirmed that PROVENANCE.md lists embedded-captions and talking-head-recut as intentionally not vendored. Upstream heygen-com/hyperframes is Apache-2.0 with 52,708 stars, and its skills/embedded-captions contains dna/, modes/, themes/, scripts/ and CATALOG.md.
captions_detail:
Code path:
1. tools/analysis/transcriber.py: faster-whisper, model 'base' by default, word_timestamps=True, vad_filter=True. The language is auto-detected or given as an ISO code, so Spanish works. WhisperX diarization is optional.
2. tools/video/remotion_caption_burn.py: applies a corrections dictionary with punctuation preserved, converts to WordCaption[] (SRT input is split evenly into fake word timings), copies the video into remotion-composer/public/talking-head, writes props with only videoSrc, captions, overlays, wordsPerPage, fontSize and highlightColor, then runs `npx remotion render TalkingHead --width/--height from ffprobe --fps=30 --frames=0-(dur*30-1) --codec=h264 --crf=18`.
3. TalkingHead.tsx, then CaptionOverlay.tsx.

The look:
- Pages of 4 words in the talking-head path (the component default is 6) inside a rounded rgba(0,0,0,0.65) box, max 80% width, fontWeight 700.
- The page springs in with opacity and translateY 20 to 0.
- The active word gets highlightColor (default #22D3EE) and a 20px glow; past words are white; upcoming words are white at 60% alpha.
- Fixed bottom placement (paddingBottom 80).

Missing:
- Per-word scale, pop or bounce.
- Keyword or LLM emphasis.
- Emoji.
- Named presets.
- Stroke, outline or uppercase styles.
- Face or safe-zone placement.
- Line or page animation variety.
- Tool-level control of color, background or font, even though the component supports them.

Fallbacks: the FFmpeg path burns SRT with force_style (Segoe UI 24 bold, outline 3, MarginV 100) in 4-word chunks. subtitle_gen.py emits SRT, VTT or JSON.

@remotion/captions is listed in package.json but not imported anywhere in src. The vendored HyperFrames caption-skin.html presets under .agents/skills/hyperframes-creative/frame-presets/ need captions.mjs, which is absent, and the tool states that HyperFrames word-level captions are deferred.

Verdict: the same basic tier as the user's autobroll captions. The candidate premium donor is upstream heygen-com/hyperframes skills/embedded-captions (Apache-2.0), which has not been evaluated.

llm_integration_detail:
No LLM is hard-wired. Code search finds no anthropic SDK, OpenAI chat or responses calls, or MCP server. The openai and google-genai packages are used only for media generation (Sora, Veo, Lyria, Imagen), and video_understand uses local transformers.

How an agent is wired in:
- Entry files: CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md say only 'MANDATORY: Read AGENT_GUIDE.md'. CODEX.md points to AGENT_GUIDE.md and PROJECT_CONTEXT.md. CURSOR.md, COPILOT.md, .windsurfrules and .cursor/rules/openmontage.mdc are also present.
- Skill mirrors: .claude/skills and .agents/skills, plus .codex/prompts and .cursor/commands with 3 niche commands each.
- The agent reads the 48 KB AGENT_GUIDE.md, runs `python -c` snippets for registry.discover(), provider_menu() and init_project(), picks a pipeline YAML, follows skills/pipelines/<pipeline>/*-director.md, calls Tool().execute({...}) to get a ToolResult, and writes checkpoints through lib/checkpoint.py.
- write_checkpoint validates artifact JSON schemas and enforces predecessor completion and approval.
- Backlot shows progress read-only.

This is exactly a 'Claude Code or Codex CLI as brain' design. Weaknesses:
- It depends on the agent obeying long prose.
- There are no typed tool calls or MCP.
- Tool inputs are not schema-validated at execute time.
- Approval flags are set by the agent.
- There is no harness for testing whole agent runs.
license_risks:
1. The whole repo is AGPL-3.0. Copying any OpenMontage-authored code, components or skills makes the user's editor AGPL, and a hosted service must offer source to its network users. Reimplementing the ideas is safe.
2. Remotion (^4.0.484) uses the Remotion License, which is source-available, not OSI open source. It is free for individuals, for-profit companies with up to 3 employees, non-profits and evaluation. Anyone else needs a Company License (priced at remotion.pro; automated or server-side rendering has its own pricing). It also forbids selling or relicensing a derivative of Remotion itself, and its terms change in Remotion 5.0. OpenMontage's README does not mention this.
3. GSAP 3.14.2 is loaded from the jsDelivr CDN under the GSAP Standard License, which is free but prohibits use in no-code visual animation builders that compete with Webflow. This matters if the user's editor exposes visual animation authoring.
4. The HyperFrames CLI (npm `hyperframes`, fetched at runtime) and the vendored skills are Apache-2.0 from heygen-com/hyperframes. Take them from upstream to keep provenance clean and avoid AGPL entanglement.
5. The vendored SFX are under the Pixabay Content License, which allows commercial use but restricts standalone redistribution. Bundling the raw files in a product repo is a grey area; use them only inside rendered outputs, or re-source them.
6. Other material:
   - Manim skills carry their own LICENSE.txt.
   - ink-theater bundles OFL fonts and CMU mocap data (see ink-theater/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).
   - CLIP ViT-B/32 weights are MIT, and faster-whisper is MIT.
   - WhisperX diarization pulls gated pyannote models with their own terms.
   - The many cloud-provider wrappers are each subject to that provider's terms of service.

summary:
**What it is:** a Claude Code skill pack (SKILL.md procedures plus helper CLI scripts), not an editor app or library. A Claude Code session reads the skills, runs the Python/Node scripts, and writes the HyperFrames HTML/GSAP composition for each video by hand.

**What I confirmed in the code:**
- A careful cutting and seam toolchain:
  - plan_cuts.py: a VAD residual-gap join planner with noise-floor edge walking, flub-segment drop and nudges.
  - cut_timeline.py: a lossless cutter on a frame and audio-sample grid (FFV1/PCM batches of 16, one AAC encode) that verifies its own output.
  - remap-transcript.py: remaps transcripts through the edit list.
  - tools/video-qa layer1: ffmpeg black/freeze/flash detection, EBU R128 loudness and true peak.
  - tools/video-qa layer2: checks for clipped words, repeated words, seam dead air and butt-splice clicks.
- A large but one-off GSAP motion vocabulary: 36 primitive functions inside build-comp.mjs, plus a PUNCH camera helper on the generator side.
- A tested review canvas with frame-pinned notes and version compare.

**Absent:**
- color grading;
- stock B-roll search (no Pexels);
- filler-word removal from the audio (fillers are dropped only from caption text);
- automatic bad-take scoring (retakes are found by the LLM plus a manual flubs.json);
- Spanish support (English is hard-coded in several transcription paths).

**Captions (the user's question):** this repo does NOT close the gap to premium captions.
- generate-captions.mjs calls itself a "karaoke caption generator", but it only pops whole chunks of 1–3 words in, with opacity and scale 0.92→1. Keywords are colored by a regex, and the color itself is set by hand-entered time ranges.
- build_reel.py's caption_layer docstring also says "Karaoke caption", but it draws a static PIL text image.
- The only per-word pop, boxed-word styling and caption muting live in the one-project build-comp.mjs.
- There is no active-word highlight in the generic path, no emoji, no preset library and no automatic emphasis.

This is roughly the same "basic highlight" tier AutoBroll already has, so it gives no premium-caption code to borrow.

**License:** it has none, so it can serve only as a design reference.
captions_detail:
I verified three caption implementations.

**(1) branded-ad-edit/scripts/generate-captions.mjs (5.7 KB, the only generic one).**
- Merges words that ASR split, clamps the last word to the composition duration, and groups words into chunks of at most maxWordsPerChunk (default 3). A chunk breaks on a gap longer than gapBreak (0.45s) or on trailing punctuation.
- Display windows run from the chunk's start minus 0.04s to the next chunk's start minus 0.04s.
- Emits, per chunk, tl.set visible → tl.fromTo {opacity 0, scale 0.92} → {1, 1} over 0.12s power2.out → hide.
- Tokens matching a config regex are wrapped in <em class=r|g|b>, with the class picked from hand-entered colorRanges.
- The placement mode (split/solo/fullhim/full) comes from hand-entered modeRanges mapped to fixed top px in the CSS.
- It warns when caption windows overlap.
- The header calls it a "karaoke caption generator", but no per-word timing is emitted at all.

**(2) reel-recut/scripts/build_reel.py caption_layer() (line 155).** It renders each phrase once as a static PIL RGBA image: variable-font weight, fit_wrap auto-shrink, stroke of 11px by default, soft shadow, bottom third. The style is overridable through the spec's "style" block. There is no animation, although the docstring says "Karaoke caption".

**(3) arcads-video-edit/scripts/build-comp.mjs lines 520–553 plus the CSS at about line 672 (one project only).**
- 1–3 word chunks that split on shot change, a gap over 0.22s, or a span over 1.5s.
- A per-word HIT tween at each word's start (opacity 1, scale 0.92→1 back.out(2), settling to 0.9).
- Uppercase words, each on a black box (box-decoration-break), with an inverted cream variant inside capBand windows.
- The y-position comes from freespace layouts.
- A caption is muted when its significant non-stopword words already appear in an on-screen graphic's text.
- This is the closest thing to Submagic-style captions in the repo, but it is hard-wired to one project's files.

talking-head-image-overlays/references/style-system.md describes a karaoke style that boxes every word in spoken order and snaps between words, but only as prose; the skill's scripts are only face-landmark and face-band measurement tools. There are no emoji in any caption path (emoji appear only as a missing-glyph fallback and as an 'emoji tiles' card idea in example.md).

**Verdict:** this is well below Captions.ai or Submagic, and it gives no premium-caption code to reuse.
motion_graphics_detail:
**Engine:** HyperFrames, which renders HTML plus one paused GSAP timeline registered on window.__timelines to MP4 in headless Chrome. It is external: the pack says to install it with `npx hyperframes`, and gsap.min.js is pulled via `npx hyperframes skills update talking-head-recut`. Every graphic is written per project by the LLM or in a per-project generator; there is no template library.

**Generic path: branded-ad-edit/assets/index-template-starter.html.**
- «FILL» markers for the parts the LLM completes.
- Five helpers: enter, exit, pop, rise, countUp.
- Framing wrappers, a progress bar, and a commented zoom-punch recipe.
- references/design.md §4 gives 12 card archetypes as a prose table only (stamp, count-up, before/after, word-synced chips, icon tiles, strikethrough list, one-word takeover, SVG ring timer, brand reveal in a browser frame, social proof, guarantee shield, CTA).
- There are zero packaged card components.

**One-off: arcads-video-edit/scripts/build-comp.mjs.**
- The JS block at about lines 677–722 defines 36 GSAP primitive functions: SLAM, SLAMW, QUOTES, RISEW, WATER, ROLL, HANG, POPC, OUTC, UPOUT, GRAV, TICK, EXTRUDE, SHEEN, SHEENRAIL, DRAWP, FLOW, PACKET, RADAR, HALO, TOGGLE, buildDots, CHECK (particles plus counter), TYPE, BLINK, STREAM, WAVE, TUMBLE, JITTER, WEIGHTS, SLOTSWAP, BLINDS, SLICEIN, WHIP, STACKTO, CAP and HIT.
- It also has a generator-side PUNCH zoom with the transform origin placed on the face (lines 55–60), a three-wrapper camera (clip-path, move/scale, punch), a circle PIP, takeovers, and SFX hits placed on words.
- The craft is high and pro-looking in intent, but the file reads project-specific inputs (mg/words.json, qa/v5-timeline.json, mg/freespace.json), hard-codes DUR=93.5 and looks up spoken words ("easiest", "comment"). It is not reusable as is.

**Other:**
- reel-recut: static PIL banner and callout boxes, composited into one qtrle ARGB overlay.
- openart-broll: a prompt contract only, with no code.
- freespace.py: real subject-avoiding placement (temporal-max Sobel importance plus a temporal-std subject box), but also hard-coded to one file.

There are no lower-third, UI-mockup, icon or animated-stat component libraries shipped as code; output quality depends entirely on the LLM for each video.
llm_integration_detail:
**The brain is a Claude Code session.**
- CLAUDE.md sets session rules and routes every edit request to the video-edit-pipeline skill, which orchestrates 18 specialist skills.
- scripts/setup.py link_skills() symlinks every skill directory into `<working-repo>/.claude/skills` only.
- CLAUDE.md states "No MCP servers are required by this pack"; the OpenArt MCP is an optional client-side connector for B-roll.
- No LLM API is hard-coded for editing decisions.

summary:
This is a small, well-documented Claude Code skill, not an app. Claude reads SKILL.md and runs the deterministic scripts (prep, transcribe, cut, stills, render). It picks the best take of each sentence from the printed whisper segment table, writes reel-segments.json by hand, and then hand-writes a Remotion TSX timeline (Reel.tsx) that places prebuilt overlay components at original-recording seconds.

Verified in code:
(1) Cutting. cut.py keeps a word when at least min(0.1 s, half the word) overlaps a take. It frame-snaps the take lengths, remaps words to edit time and applies word and phrase fixes. Reel.tsx plays each take as an OffthreadVideo with 2-frame fade-in and 3-frame fade-out audio. The choice of takes is 100% LLM judgment. There is no automatic detection of silence or filler words.
(2) There is no colour grading.
(3) Captions are the basic tier. ReelCaptions shows 3-word groups in a dark pill, with the current word in #FFD166 at a static scale(1.06).
(4) There is no stock b-roll code. Memes from imgflip exist only as an instruction to the LLM.
(5) Motion graphics are the real strength. There are 13 documented vertical overlays in reel-overlays.tsx, plus Card, Big and LogoRow from overlays.tsx, for about 16 live templates. They use spring animations and have SFX wired in. useZoom adds snap and push zooms.

On the user's actual question (autobroll has captions, but not Captions.ai-level ones): this repo does not close that gap. Its captions are the same "highlight the current word" tier. There are no presets, no per-word entrance animation, no keyword emphasis, no in-caption emoji and no Spanish, because whisper is forced to --language en. Premium captions still have to be built. At most, ReelCaptions is a 75-line starting point for a Remotion caption component. The repo's value is the overlay component library, the zoom grammar, the E() source-time mapper, cut.py's retiming and the editing know-how in SKILL.md.

llm_integration_detail:
This is a pure Claude Code skill. SKILL.md has name and description frontmatter with trigger phrases, and references/take-selection.md and references/layout.md are loaded on demand. Grepping the code finds no API key, SDK call, MCP server, Codex adapter or structured tool schema.

The LLM does three things:
1. Runs the bash and Python CLIs.
2. Writes remotion/src/talk/reel-segments.json by hand from the printed table.
3. Edits Reel.tsx by hand as free-form code: beats, SNAPS, PUSHES and component props.

render.sh prints a polling loop meant for Claude Code's Monitor tool, which works around the Bash tool's 10-minute limit.

Codex CLI could in principle follow the same markdown and CLIs through AGENTS.md, but nothing in the repo supports or tests that. The claim that it is "vendor-neutral in practice" is an inference, not something the repo implements.

The only guardrails are E(), which throws when a beat points at cut material, and cut.py's checks for b <= a and for a segment with no words. The cut.py docstring promises that it "fails loudly if segments overlap in edit order", but no such check exists in the code.

For a product harness where Claude and Codex must be swappable and act through deterministic tools, the output channel ("edit this TSX file") is brittle. It is non-deterministic, can fail to compile and has no JSON schema.

fit_rationale:
Use it as a donor, not a base. It covers maybe a third of the goal: LLM-guided retake selection with word-accurate cut math, and a tasteful but narrow Remotion overlay kit with SFX and zoom punches. It has no colour grading, no stock b-roll, no automatic silence or filler removal and no Spanish, and its captions are the basic tier the user explicitly rejects. It is therefore no answer to "autobroll's captions aren't premium enough".

Architecturally, the LLM hand-writes TSX for every reel instead of calling structured deterministic tools. That is the opposite of the target harness (LLM brain plus deterministic tools, Claude or Codex swappable). Forking it would mean replacing that layer with a JSON edit schema or MCP and building everything else around it.

If the user already has autobroll with an MCP (add_caption, add_broll, search_stock, render and so on), the sensible move is to lift the overlay components as parameterized templates, useZoom, E(), cut.py's retiming rule, make_sfx.py, stills.sh and the beat table and layout know-how. Premium captions (per-word animation presets, emphasis, emoji, es/en) must be built regardless. Account for Remotion company-license exposure if autobroll is not already on Remotion.

summary: Confirmed: video-use is a skill, not an app. SKILL.md is symlinked into ~/.claude/skills or ~/.codex/skills and drives 6 ffmpeg helper CLIs. The code makes no LLM API calls. The only external API is ElevenLabs Scribe. The agent reads a phrase-level packed transcript and hand-writes edl.json. render.py then extracts each range (grade, HDR tonemap and 30ms afades baked in), concatenates with -c copy, overlays clips full-frame with a PTS shift, burns a 2-word UPPERCASE SRT through libass with one hard-coded style, and runs two-pass loudnorm to -14 LUFS. Cutting uses no deterministic silence or filler detector: the LLM makes every call, guided by prose rules. Grading is 3 non-empty ffmpeg presets plus a bounded signalstats auto-correction. Captions are basic and static: no per-word animation, highlight, emphasis, emoji or presets. There is no stock B-roll code. Motion graphics have no templates or generator code: SKILL.md only tells sub-agents to write HyperFrames/Remotion/Manim/PIL code from scratch, and render.py can only composite the result full-frame at 0,0, with transparent WebM overlays probably losing alpha. There is no editor UI in main. The strong parts are the agent-agnostic skill + CLI harness pattern and careful ffmpeg ingest/render details (HDR tonemap, rotation-aware portrait detection, fps preservation, fades, loudnorm). On the user's question: video-use would not give autobroll premium captions. Its captions are below the "highlight one word" baseline the user already rejects.

scores.evidence: helpers/render.py extract_segment() (lines 234-300) cuts each EDL range with -ss before -i and -t, re-encodes with libx264 and bakes in afade in/out of 30ms. concat_segments() (371-387) joins them with the concat demuxer and -c copy. helpers/transcribe.py call_scribe() posts to ElevenLabs Scribe with model_id=scribe_v1, timestamps_granularity=word, diarize and tag_audio_events. helpers/pack_transcripts.py group_into_phrases() breaks on 'spacing' gaps of 0.5s or more or on a speaker change and emits [start-end] phrase lines. SKILL.md 'Cut craft' and Hard Rules 6-7 cover word-boundary snapping and 30-200ms padding.
scores.notes: The cut mechanics work. All detection is LLM judgment: no VAD, filler list, retake scoring or EDL validation (nothing checks overlaps, end>start or word-boundary snapping). The packed view carries timestamps only at phrase edges, so removing an 'um' mid-phrase requires the LLM to read the raw Scribe JSON. That contradicts the README's 'word-boundary precision from text alone'. transcribe.py's docstring says 'verbatim', but call_scribe sends no verbatim or disfluency parameter, so whether fillers are kept depends on Scribe's default behavior (unverified).

scores.evidence: helpers/grade.py PRESETS has 4 entries: subtle (eq), neutral_punch (eq + curves), warm_cinematic (eq + colorbalance + curves) and none (empty). _sample_frame_stats() runs ffmpeg fps + signalstats + metadata=print, parses YAVG/YMIN/YMAX/SATAVG and normalizes by YBITDEPTH. auto_grade_for_clip() emits an eq with contrast, gamma and saturation clamped to contrast 0.94-1.08, gamma 0.94-1.10 and saturation 0.94-1.06. render.py resolve_grade_filter() accepts a preset, a raw filter string or 'auto' (resolved per segment), and extract_segment() prepends TONEMAP_CHAIN (zscale + hable) for HLG/PQ sources.
scores.notes: A real but basic implementation. There is no LUT workflow (a raw lut3d= string can be passed through), no white balance, no skin-tone protection and no shot matching. Auto-grade samples the source before tonemapping, so for iPhone HLG footage the statistics come from HDR code values rather than the SDR output. The docstring says ±8%, but the gamma clamp allows +10%.

captions_detail: All caption code is in helpers/render.py. build_master_srt() takes Scribe 'word' tokens inside each EDL range and remaps them to output time (word.start - seg_start + seg_offset, so they stay correct after cuts). It chunks every 2 words or at punctuation, uppercases, strips trailing ,;: and writes a plain SRT. build_final_composite() burns that SRT last with ffmpeg's libass `subtitles` filter and one constant SUB_FORCE_STYLE: Helvetica 18 Bold, white, 2px black outline, bottom-center, MarginV=90 for the Reels/TikTok safe zone. There is no ASS output, no \k karaoke, no active-word color, no scale/pop/bounce, no emphasis detection, no emoji, no presets, no per-speaker style and no animated placement. Each 2-word cue is static. SKILL.md invites the LLM to 'invent' styles, but the code has no hook for that beyond editing the constant or supplying your own subtitle file. Latent bug: the transcript lookup uses transcripts/<EDL source key>.json, so segments transcribed with --audio-track N (written as <stem>.trackN.json) silently get no captions. On the user's question ("what if autobroll has captions but they're not premium like captions.ai"): video-use does not fix that. Its captions are weaker than a highlight-one-word system. The only transferable idea is the cut-aware word-time remap, which autobroll probably already has. Premium per-word animated captions (ASS karaoke/transform tags, or a Remotion or HyperFrames caption layer with emphasis and emoji) would have to come from another candidate or be built. Community PRs #159 (+210, EDL-configurable chunking and style) and #168 (+5.8k, styled caption images and measured word cards) try parts of this, but both are open and unmerged.
motion_graphics_detail: The repo contains no motion-graphics code or templates. SKILL.md tells the main agent to spawn one parallel sub-agent per animation slot through Claude Code's Agent tool. Each gets a self-contained brief (resolution, fps, codec, palette, font path, a frame-by-frame timeline with easing, an anti-list, "do not ask questions"), and the sub-agent writes new code in one of four ways. HyperFrames (`npx --yes hyperframes init/lint/validate/render`, WebM when alpha is needed). Remotion (`npx create-video@latest`, project-local `remotion render`). Manim, using the vendored skills/manim-video prompt pack, which is byte-identical in its README to NousResearch/hermes-agent's skills/creative/manim-video. Or PIL PNG sequences through ffmpeg, which is what the authors' launch video used (orange-on-black terminal cards). The guidance is sensible: cubic easing, landing the reveal on the payoff word's timestamp, holding at least 1s, one reveal at a time, and anchoring typewriter text to the full string. It is still only prose. render.py composites each clip with setpts PTS shift + overlay enable=between, always at 0,0, with no scale, position, blend mode or SFX track. The default render.mp4 is opaque, so overlays act as full-screen cutaways. For transparent WebM, ffmpeg's native VP9 decoder drops alpha unless libvpx-vp9 is forced before -i, and render.py does not do that (inferred, not executed). Quality is unbounded but not repeatable, every reel pays full LLM generation cost and latency, and nothing reusable ships: no kinetic-type library, stat counters, icons, lower-thirds, UI mockups, zoom punches or SFX.
llm_integration_detail: Integration is purely skill-based. The code makes no LLM API or SDK calls. install.md registers the whole repo by symlink into ~/.claude/skills/video-use (Claude Code) or ${CODEX_HOME:-~/.codex}/skills/video-use (Codex); other agents import SKILL.md into their system prompt. SKILL.md (frontmatter name/description) is the orchestration layer: 12 Hard Rules, the process (inventory, pre-scan, converse, propose, wait for approval, execute, preview, self-eval up to 3 passes, persist to project.md), an editor sub-agent brief that returns EDL JSON, and a parallel animation sub-agent brief. The agent calls `python helpers/*.py` through its shell tool. It 'sees' video through takes_packed.md (phrase-level text with timestamps) and on-demand timeline_view PNGs. There is no MCP server, no typed tool definitions, no EDL schema or validation, and no deterministic guardrail beyond render.py's mechanics. Correctness rests on the model following prose rules. Hard Rule 10 names Claude Code's `Agent` tool, so parallel sub-agents are Claude-flavored and on Codex that rule cannot be followed as written. ElevenLabs Scribe is hard-wired (ELEVENLABS_API_KEY from .env or the environment), and SKILL.md discourages local Whisper. The pattern maps directly onto the user's 'Claude Code or Codex as the brain over deterministic tools' idea, but a production harness would want an MCP or typed CLI layer with schema validation on top.
license_risks: (1) The repo is MIT (LICENSE added 2026-05-10 via PR #32; pyproject points to it) with no bundled binaries. (2) The vendored skills/manim-video/ was copied from NousResearch/hermes-agent skills/creative/manim-video: the README is byte-identical, including the stale `skills/creative/manim-video/scripts/setup.sh` path, and it was added there 2026-04-04, 8 days before video-use existed. Upstream is MIT, but video-use ships it without Nous Research's copyright notice. That is a minor attribution gap to fix before redistributing. (3) ElevenLabs Scribe is a paid proprietary API and a hard dependency for transcription, with no offline fallback. (4) Remotion is one of the suggested engines, installed per slot by npx. Its LICENSE.md is free for individuals and for-profit organizations with up to 3 employees; larger for-profits need a company license. video-use does not bundle it, so exposure depends on whether the agent picks Remotion. (5) HyperFrames (heygen-com/hyperframes) is Apache-2.0, but `npx --yes` pulls unpinned versions at render time. (6) Manim CE is MIT, but its path needs a multi-GB LaTeX install.
